verses.1:1: The wisdom of many and great things has been shown to us through the law and the prophets and others who followed them, in which it is fitting to praise Israel for the sake of instruction and wisdom, because not only must the speakers themselves be skilled, but even outsiders can become most learned both by speaking and by writing. My grandfather Jesus, after he gave himself more fully to the diligent reading of the law and the prophets and the other books that were handed down to us by our forefathers, wished himself also to write something of these things that pertain to instruction and wisdom, so that those who desire to learn, having become skilled in them, may pay closer and closer attention in mind and be strengthened for a lawful life. Therefore I urge you to come with goodwill, and to read with more attentive zeal, and to grant indulgence in those places where we seem, while following the image of wisdom, to fall short in the phrasing of words. For Hebrew words fall short when they are translated into another language; and not only these, but even the law itself, and the prophets, and the rest of the other books have no small difference when they are spoken in themselves. For in the thirty-eighth year, in the times of King Ptolemy Euergetes, after I arrived in Egypt and had been there a long time, I found books left there of no small and no contemptible instruction. Therefore I thought it good and necessary for me myself also to add some diligence and labor in translating this book; and with much watchfulness I brought instruction over a span of time, to give this book for those things that lead to the end, and to those who wish to apply their mind and to learn how one ought to order conduct, who have resolved to live life according to the law of the Lord. All wisdom is from the Lord God, and was with Him always, and is before eternity.
verses.1:2: Who has counted the sand of the sea, and the drops of rain, and the days of the age? Who has measured the height of heaven, and the width of the earth, and the depth of the abyss?
verses.1:3: Who has searched out the wisdom of God, which precedes all things?
verses.1:4: Before all things wisdom was created, and understanding of prudence from eternity.
verses.1:5: The spring of wisdom is the word of God on high, and her approaches are eternal commandments.
verses.1:6: To whom has the root of wisdom been revealed? And who has recognized her subtleties?
verses.1:7: To whom has the instruction of wisdom been revealed and made plain? And who has understood the multiplicity of her approach?
verses.1:8: There is one Most High, almighty Creator, and a mighty King and exceedingly to be feared, sitting upon His throne, and a ruling God.
verses.1:9: He Himself created her in the Holy Spirit, and saw, and counted, and measured her,
verses.1:10: and poured her out upon all His works, and upon all flesh, according to His gift, and granted her to those who love Him.
verses.1:11: The fear of the Lord is glory, and glorying, and gladness, and a crown of exultation.
verses.1:12: The fear of the Lord will delight the heart, and will give gladness, and joy, and length of days.
verses.1:13: For the one who fears the Lord, it will be well at the end, and on the day of his death he will be blessed.
verses.1:14: The love of God is honorable wisdom,
verses.1:15: and those to whom she appears in a vision love her in the vision and in the knowledge of her great works.
verses.1:16: The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord, and it was created together with the faithful in the womb; it walks with chosen women, and is recognized with the righteous and faithful.
verses.1:17: The fear of the Lord is the piety of knowledge;
verses.1:18: piety will guard and justify the heart; it will give delight and joy.
verses.1:19: For the one who fears the Lord, it will be well, and in the days of his completion he will be blessed.
verses.1:20: The fullness of wisdom is to fear God, and fullness is from her fruits.
verses.1:21: She will fill her entire house with produce, and the storerooms with her treasures.
verses.1:22: The crown of wisdom is the fear of the Lord, replenishing peace and the fruit of salvation.
verses.1:23: And He saw and counted her; moreover, both are gifts of God.
verses.1:24: Wisdom will share out knowledge and the understanding of prudence, and she exalts the glory of those who hold fast to her.
verses.1:25: The root of wisdom is to fear the Lord, and her branches are long-lived.
verses.1:26: In the treasuries of wisdom are understanding and the piety of knowledge, but to sinners wisdom is an abomination.
verses.1:27: The fear of the Lord drives out sin.
verses.1:28: For the one who is without fear will not be able to be justified; for the wrath of his temper is his downfall.
verses.1:29: For a time the patient one will endure, and afterward there is a return of delight.
verses.1:30: Good judgment will hide his words for a time, and the lips of many will recount his judgment.
verses.1:31: In the treasuries of wisdom is the indication of discipline,
verses.1:32: but to a sinner the worship of God is an abomination.
verses.1:33: Son, desiring wisdom, keep righteousness, and God will grant her to you.
verses.1:34: For the fear of the Lord is wisdom and discipline; and what is well-pleasing to Him
verses.1:35: is faith and gentleness, and He will fill his treasuries.
verses.1:36: Do not be distrustful of the fear of the Lord, and do not approach Him with a double heart.
verses.1:37: Do not be a hypocrite in the sight of men, and do not be made to stumble by your lips.
verses.1:38: Pay attention to them, or else you might fall, and bring dishonor upon your soul,
verses.1:39: and God might reveal your hidden things, and dash you down in the midst of the assembly,
verses.1:40: because you approached the Lord wickedly, and your heart is full of deceit and falsehood.
verses.2:1: Son, approaching the service of God, stand in righteousness and fear, and prepare your soul for temptation.
verses.2:2: Humble your heart, and endure; incline your ear, and receive words of understanding; and do not hasten in the time of calamity.
verses.2:3: Endure the delays of God; be joined to God, and endure, so that your life may increase at the last.
verses.2:4: Accept everything that is laid upon you, and in sorrow endure, and in your lowliness have patience,
verses.2:5: for in fire gold and silver are tested, and acceptable men in the furnace of humiliation.
verses.2:6: Believe God, and He will restore you; and direct your way, and hope in Him; keep His fear, and grow old in it.
verses.2:7: You who fear the Lord, wait for His mercy, and do not turn aside from Him, so that you do not fall.
verses.2:8: You who fear the Lord, believe Him, and your reward will not be made void.
verses.2:9: You who fear the Lord, hope in Him, and mercy will come to you for delight.
verses.2:10: You who fear the Lord, love Him, and your hearts will be enlightened.
verses.2:11: Look, sons, at the nations of men, and know that no one has hoped in the Lord and been put to shame.
verses.2:12: For who has remained in His commandments and been abandoned? Or who has called upon Him, and He despised him?
verses.2:13: For God is compassionate and merciful, and will forgive sins in the day of tribulation, and is a protector to all who seek Him in truth.
verses.2:14: Woe to the double-hearted, and to wicked lips, and to hands that do evil, and to the sinner who walks the earth by two ways!
verses.2:15: Woe to those faint in heart, who do not believe God, and therefore will not be protected by Him!
verses.2:16: Woe to those who have lost endurance, and who have abandoned straight ways, and turned aside into crooked ways!
verses.2:17: And what will they do when the Lord begins to inspect?
verses.2:18: Those who fear the Lord will not be distrustful of His word, and those who love Him will keep His way.
verses.2:19: Those who fear the Lord will seek out the things that are well-pleasing to Him, and those who love Him will be filled with His law.
verses.2:20: Those who fear the Lord will prepare their hearts, and in His sight will sanctify their souls.
verses.2:21: Those who fear the Lord keep His commandments, and they will remain patient until His visitation,
verses.2:22: saying, "If we do not repent, we will fall into the hands of the Lord, and not into the hands of men.
verses.2:23: For according to His greatness, so also is His mercy with Him."
verses.3:1: The children of wisdom are the assembly of the righteous, and their nation is obedience and love.
verses.3:2: Hear the judgment of a father, children, and act in this way, so that you may be saved.
verses.3:3: For God honored the father in the children, and seeking out the judgment of the mother, He established it upon the children.
verses.3:4: He who loves God will make entreaty for sins, and will restrain himself from them, and in daily prayer he will be heard.
verses.3:5: And just as one who stores up treasure, so also is he who honors his mother.
verses.3:6: He who honors his father will rejoice in his children, and on the day of his prayer he will be heard.
verses.3:7: He who honors his father will live a longer life, and he who obeys his father will refresh his mother.
verses.3:8: He who fears the Lord honors his parents, and will serve as masters those who brought him forth.
verses.3:9: In deed, and speech, and all patience, honor your father,
verses.3:10: so that a blessing from him may come upon you, and his blessing may remain at the end.
verses.3:11: The blessing of a father establishes the houses of children, but the curse of a mother uproots the foundations.
verses.3:12: Do not glory in the dishonor of your father, for his shame is not glory to you.
verses.3:13: For the glory of a man is from the honor of his father, and the disgrace of a son is a father without honor.
verses.3:14: Son, support the old age of your father, and do not grieve him during his life;
verses.3:15: and if he fails in understanding, grant him pardon, and do not despise him in your strength; for almsgiving to a father will not be forgotten.
verses.3:16: For in place of a mother's sin, good will be restored to you;
verses.3:17: and in righteousness it will be built up for you, and on the day of tribulation you will be remembered, and like ice in clear weather, your sins will dissolve.
verses.3:18: How bad is the reputation of the one who abandons his father, and cursed by God is the one who provokes his mother!
verses.3:19: Son, accomplish your works in gentleness, and you will be loved above the glory of men.
verses.3:20: However great you are, humble yourself in all things, and before God you will find favor;
verses.3:21: for great is the power of God alone, and by the humble He is honored.
verses.3:22: Do not seek things too high for you, and do not search into things too strong for you; but the things that God has commanded you, think about those always, and do not be inquisitive about too many of His works.
verses.3:23: For it is not necessary for you to see with your eyes the things that are hidden.
verses.3:24: Do not search in many ways into unnecessary matters, and you will not be inquisitive about too many of His works.
verses.3:25: For very many things beyond the understanding of men have been shown to you;
verses.3:26: their own conjecture has also tripped up many, and has held their minds in emptiness.
verses.3:27: A hard heart will fare poorly in the end, and the one who loves danger will perish in it.
verses.3:28: A heart entering upon two ways will not have success, and the one who is crooked in heart will stumble in them.
verses.3:29: A wicked heart will be weighed down with sorrows, and the sinner will add to his sinning.
verses.3:30: For the assembly of the proud there will be no healing, for the shoot of sin will take root in them, and it will not be understood.
verses.3:31: The heart of a wise man is understood in wisdom, and a good ear will hear wisdom with all desire.
verses.3:32: A wise and discerning heart will keep itself from sins, and in deeds of righteousness it will have success.
verses.3:33: Water extinguishes a burning fire, and almsgiving resists sins;
verses.3:34: and God is the watcher over him who returns a favor: He remembers him for the future, and in the time of his fall he will find firm support.
verses.4:1: Son, do not defraud a poor man of his alms, and do not turn your eyes away from a poor man.
verses.4:2: Do not despise a hungry soul, and do not provoke a poor man in his need.
verses.4:3: Do not afflict the heart of a needy man, and do not delay a gift to one in distress.
verses.4:4: Do not reject the petition of the sorely afflicted, and do not turn your face away from a destitute man.
verses.4:5: Do not turn your eyes away from a needy man because of anger, and do not leave it to those who ask to curse you behind your back.
verses.4:6: For the supplication of one who curses you in the bitterness of his soul will be heard; and He who made him will hear him.
verses.4:7: Make yourself approachable to the congregation of the poor, and humble your soul before an elder, and bow your head before a great man.
verses.4:8: Incline your ear to a poor man without sadness, and pay your debt, and answer him with peaceful words in gentleness.
verses.4:9: Deliver the one who suffers wrong from the hand of the proud, and do not take it bitterly in your soul.
verses.4:10: In judging, be merciful to orphans like a father, and in place of a husband to their mother.
verses.4:11: And you will be like an obedient son of the Most High, and He will have mercy on you more than a mother.
verses.4:12: Wisdom breathes life into her children, and supports those who seek her, and will go ahead in the way of righteousness.
verses.4:13: And he who loves her loves life, and those who keep watch for her will embrace her delight.
verses.4:14: Those who hold fast to her will inherit life, and whatever place she enters, God will bless.
verses.4:15: Those who serve her will be obedient to the Holy One, and those who love her, God loves.
verses.4:16: He who hears her will judge the nations, and he who gazes upon her will remain confident.
verses.4:17: If he trusts her, he will inherit her, and his offspring will be in steadfastness,
verses.4:18: for in testing she walks with him, and at first she chooses him.
verses.4:19: She will bring fear and dread and testing upon him, and she will torment him in the tribulation of her instruction until she tests him in his thoughts and trusts his soul.
verses.4:20: And she will establish him, and will bring a straight path to him, and will make him glad.
verses.4:21: And she will lay bare her hidden things to him, and will treasure up upon him knowledge and the understanding of righteousness.
verses.4:22: But if he goes astray, she will abandon him, and will hand him over into the hands of his enemy.
verses.4:23: Son, observe the time, and turn aside from evil.
verses.4:24: For the sake of your soul, do not be ashamed to speak the truth.
verses.4:25: For there is a shame that brings sin, and there is a shame that brings glory and favor.
verses.4:26: Do not accept a face against your own face, nor a lie against your own soul.
verses.4:27: Do not defer to your neighbor in his fall.
verses.4:28: And do not hold back a word in a time of salvation. Do not hide your wisdom in its beauty;
verses.4:29: for in the tongue wisdom is recognized, and understanding, and knowledge, and instruction in the word of a man of understanding, and firmness in the works of righteousness.
verses.4:30: Do not contradict the word of truth in any way, and be ashamed of the lie of your ignorance.
verses.4:31: Do not be ashamed to confess your sins, and do not subject yourself to every man on account of sin.
verses.4:32: Do not resist against the face of a powerful man, and do not strive against the force of a river.
verses.4:33: Contend for righteousness on behalf of your soul, and fight for righteousness even to death, and God will conquer your enemies for you.
verses.4:34: Do not be hasty in your tongue, and useless and slack in your works.
verses.4:35: Do not be like a lion in your house, overturning those of your household, and oppressing those subject to you.
verses.4:36: Do not let your hand be stretched out for receiving, and drawn back for giving.
verses.5:1: Do not fix your attention on unjust possessions, and do not say, "I have enough for life," for it will profit nothing in the time of vengeance and calamity.
verses.5:2: Do not follow in your might the desire of your heart,
verses.5:3: and do not say, "How was I able?" or, "Who will subdue me because of my deeds?" For God will surely take vengeance.
verses.5:4: Do not say, "I have sinned, and what sorrowful thing has happened to me?" For the Most High is a patient repayer.
verses.5:5: Concerning a forgiven sin, do not be without fear, and do not add sin upon sin.
verses.5:6: And do not say, "The mercy of the Lord is great; He will have mercy on the multitude of my sins."
verses.5:7: For mercy and wrath draw near swiftly from Him, and His wrath looks upon sinners.
verses.5:8: Do not delay turning to the Lord, and do not put it off from day to day.
verses.5:9: For suddenly His wrath will come, and in the time of vengeance He will destroy you.
verses.5:10: Do not be anxious over unjust riches, for they will not profit you in the day of calamity and vengeance.
verses.5:11: Do not winnow yourself in every wind, and do not go along every way; for thus every sinner is proved by a double tongue.
verses.5:12: Be firm in the way of the Lord, and in the truth of your mind and knowledge; and may the word of peace and righteousness accompany you.
verses.5:13: Be gentle in hearing the word, so that you may understand, and with wisdom bring forth a true answer.
verses.5:14: If you have understanding, answer your neighbor; but if not, let your hand be upon your mouth, so that you are not caught in an undisciplined word and put to shame.
verses.5:15: Honor and glory are in the speech of a discerning person; but the tongue of an imprudent person is his own ruin.
verses.5:16: Do not be called a whisperer, and do not be caught by your tongue and put to shame;
verses.5:17: for upon a thief are shame and remorse, and the worst condemnation upon the double-tongued; but to the whisperer belong hatred and enmity and dishonor.
verses.5:18: Do justice to small and great alike.
verses.6:1: Do not become an enemy to your neighbor instead of a friend; for an evil person will inherit reproach and dishonor, as will every envious and double-tongued sinner.
verses.6:2: Do not exalt yourself in the thought of your soul like a bull, or else your strength may be crushed through folly,
verses.6:3: and it may devour your leaves and destroy your fruits, and you may be left like a dry tree in the wilderness.
verses.6:4: For a wicked soul will destroy the one who possesses it, and gives him as a joy to enemies, and will lead him down into the lot of the ungodly.
verses.6:5: A sweet word multiplies friends and appeases enemies, and a gracious tongue abounds in a good person.
verses.6:6: Let many be at peace with you, and let your counselor be one out of a thousand.
verses.6:7: If you acquire a friend, acquire him in testing, and do not easily trust him.
verses.6:8: For there is a friend according to his own time, and he will not remain in the day of tribulation.
verses.6:9: And there is a friend who turns to enmity, and there is a friend who will expose hatred and strife and insults.
verses.6:10: And there is a friend who is a companion of the table, and he will not remain in the day of need.
verses.6:11: If a friend remains steadfast, he will be to you like an equal, and among those of your household he will act confidently.
verses.6:12: If he humbles himself before you and hides himself from your face, you will have a good friendship of one mind.
verses.6:13: Separate yourself from your enemies, and beware of your friends.
verses.6:14: A faithful friend is a strong protection; and the one who finds him has found a treasure.
verses.6:15: There is no comparison to a faithful friend, and no weight of gold and silver is worthy compared with the goodness of his faithfulness.
verses.6:16: A faithful friend is a medicine of life and immortality; and those who fear the Lord will find him.
verses.6:17: The one who fears God will likewise have a good friendship, because his friend will be like him.
verses.6:18: Son, from your youth receive instruction, and even to gray hairs you will find wisdom.
verses.6:19: Like one who plows and sows, draw near to her, and wait for her good fruits.
verses.6:20: For in her work you will labor a little, and swiftly you will eat from her produce.
verses.6:21: How exceedingly harsh wisdom is to uninstructed people! And a senseless person will not remain in her.
verses.6:22: Like the strength of a stone, the testing will be upon them, and they will not delay to cast her off.
verses.6:23: For the wisdom of instruction is according to her name, and she is not made manifest to many; but to those by whom she is known, she remains even to the presence of God.
verses.6:24: Listen, son, and accept the counsel of understanding, and do not reject my counsel.
verses.6:25: Put your foot into her fetters, and your neck into her collar.
verses.6:26: Bow your shoulder and carry her, and do not grow weary of her bonds.
verses.6:27: With all your mind draw near to her, and with all your strength keep her ways.
verses.6:28: Search her out, and she will be made manifest to you; and once you have taken hold of her, do not abandon her;
verses.6:29: for in the end you will find rest in her, and she will be turned into delight for you.
verses.6:30: And her fetters will become for you a protection of might and foundations of strength, and her collar a robe of glory;
verses.6:31: for the beauty of life is in her, and her bonds are a saving binding.
verses.6:32: You will put her on as a robe of glory, and you will place a crown of rejoicing upon yourself.
verses.6:33: Son, if you pay attention to me, you will learn; and if you apply your mind, you will be wise.
verses.6:34: If you incline your ear, you will receive instruction; and if you love to listen, you will be wise.
verses.6:35: Stand in the multitude of prudent elders, and join yourself from the heart to their wisdom, so that you may be able to hear every account of God, and proverbs of praise may not escape from you.
verses.6:36: And if you see a discerning person, rise early to go to him, and let your foot wear away the steps of his doors.
verses.6:37: Keep your thought on the precepts of God, and in His commandments be especially diligent; and He Himself will give you a heart, and the desire for wisdom will be given to you.
verses.7:1: Do not do evil things, and they will not overtake you.
verses.7:2: Depart from what is unjust, and evil things will fall away from you.
verses.7:3: Son, do not sow evil things in the furrows of injustice, and you will not reap them sevenfold.
verses.7:4: Do not seek leadership from the Lord, nor a seat of honor from a king.
verses.7:5: Do not justify yourself before God, for He Himself is the knower of the heart; and in the presence of a king, do not wish to appear wise.
verses.7:6: Do not seek to become a judge unless you are able by strength to break through iniquities, or else you might dread the face of a powerful man and place a stumbling block in your uprightness.
verses.7:7: Do not sin against the multitude of the city, and do not thrust yourself into the people;
verses.7:8: and do not bind up double sins, for not even for one will you go unpunished.
verses.7:9: Do not be fainthearted in your mind;
verses.7:10: do not despise praying and giving alms.
verses.7:11: Do not say, "God will look upon the multitude of my gifts, and when I offer to God Most High, He will receive my gifts."
verses.7:12: Do not mock a man in bitterness of soul, for there is One who humbles and exalts: God, the all-seeing observer.
verses.7:13: Do not love a lie against your brother, nor do the same against a friend.
verses.7:14: Do not wish to tell any lie, for the continual practice of it is not good.
verses.7:15: Do not be wordy in the multitude of the elders, and do not repeat a word in your prayer.
verses.7:16: Do not hate laborious works and farming created by the Most High.
verses.7:17: Do not count yourself in the multitude of the undisciplined.
verses.7:18: Remember wrath, because it will not delay.
verses.7:19: Humble your spirit greatly, for the vengeance on the flesh of the ungodly is fire and the worm.
verses.7:20: Do not deal treacherously against a friend who delays money, nor scorn a most dear brother for gold.
verses.7:21: Do not depart from a sensible and good wife whom you have received as your portion in the fear of the Lord, for the grace of her modesty is above gold.
verses.7:22: Do not harm a servant who works in truth, nor a hired worker who gives his life.
verses.7:23: Let a sensible servant be dear to you like your own soul; do not defraud him of freedom, nor abandon him destitute.
verses.7:24: You have livestock; attend to them, and if they are useful, let them remain with you.
verses.7:25: Do you have sons? Instruct them, and bend them from their childhood.
verses.7:26: Do you have daughters? Guard their body, and do not show your cheerful face to them.
verses.7:27: Give away a daughter, and you will have done a great work; and give her to a sensible man.
verses.7:28: If you have a wife according to your soul, do not cast her away, and do not entrust yourself to a detestable one. With all your heart
verses.7:29: honor your father, and do not forget the groans of your mother.
verses.7:30: Remember that if not through them, you would not have been born, and repay them just as they also did for you.
verses.7:31: With all your soul fear the Lord, and sanctify His priests.
verses.7:32: With all your strength love Him who made you, and do not abandon His ministers.
verses.7:33: Honor God from all your soul, and hold the priests in honor, and purify yourself with the arms.
verses.7:34: Give them a share, just as it has been commanded you, of the firstfruits and of purification, and purify yourself for your negligence with a few things.
verses.7:35: The gift of your arms and the sacrifice of sanctification you will offer to the Lord, and the firstfruits of the holy things.
verses.7:36: And stretch out your hand to a poor person, so that your propitiation and blessing may be made complete.
verses.7:37: The grace of a gift is in the sight of every living person, and do not withhold grace from one who is dead.
verses.7:38: Do not be lacking in consolation for those who weep, and walk with those who mourn.
verses.7:39: Do not be reluctant to visit a sick person, for from these things you will be strengthened in love.
verses.7:40: In all your works, remember your last things, and you will never sin.
verses.8:1: Do not dispute with a powerful man, or else you might fall into his hands.
verses.8:2: Do not contend with a wealthy man, or else he might set up a lawsuit against you.
verses.8:3: For gold and silver have destroyed many, and they reach even to the heart of kings and turn it.
verses.8:4: Do not dispute with a loose-tongued man, and you will not pile wood onto his fire.
verses.8:5: Do not associate with an uneducated man, so that he does not speak ill of your lineage.
verses.8:6: Do not despise a man turning away from sin, nor reproach him; remember that we are all under correction.
verses.8:7: Do not scorn a man in his old age, for indeed some of us are growing old.
verses.8:8: Do not rejoice over your dead enemy, knowing that we all die and do not wish to become a cause of rejoicing.
verses.8:9: Do not despise the discourse of wise elders, and occupy yourself with their proverbs.
verses.8:10: For from them you will learn wisdom and the instruction of understanding, and to serve great men without reproach.
verses.8:11: Do not let the discourse of older men pass you by, for they themselves learned from their fathers.
verses.8:12: Because from them you will learn understanding, and how to give an answer in a time of need.
verses.8:13: Do not kindle the coals of sinners by rebuking them, and do not be burned by the flame of the fire of their sins.
verses.8:14: Do not stand against the face of an insolent man, so that he does not sit like one lying in ambush for your mouth.
verses.8:15: Do not lend to a man stronger than you; and if you do lend, consider it as lost.
verses.8:16: Do not give a guarantee beyond your strength; and if you do give a guarantee, think as one who will repay.
verses.8:17: Do not judge against a judge, for he judges according to what is just.
verses.8:18: Do not go on the road with a reckless man, or else he might burden you with his evils; for he himself goes according to his own will, and you will perish together with his folly.
verses.8:19: Do not make a quarrel with a hot-tempered man, and do not go into the wilderness with a reckless man; for blood is like nothing before him, and where there is no help, he will strike you down.
verses.8:20: Do not hold counsel with fools, for they will not be able to love anything except what pleases them.
verses.8:21: Do not hold counsel in the presence of a stranger, for you do not know what he will bring forth.
verses.8:22: Do not reveal your heart to every man, or else he might offer you false favor and revile you.
verses.9:1: Do not be jealous of the wife of your bosom, so that she does not show against you the malice of a wicked teaching.
verses.9:2: Do not give a woman power over your soul, so that she does not enter into your strength and you be put to shame.
verses.9:3: Do not look upon a promiscuous woman, or else you might fall into her snares.
verses.9:4: Do not stay constantly with a female dancer, nor listen to her, or else you might perish in her artfulness.
verses.9:5: Do not gaze upon a virgin, or else you might be made to stumble by her beauty.
verses.9:6: Do not give your soul to prostitutes in anything, so that you do not destroy yourself and your inheritance.
verses.9:7: Do not look around in the streets of the city, nor wander about in its squares.
verses.9:8: Turn your face away from an adorned woman, and do not gaze around at another's beauty.
verses.9:9: Because of the beauty of a woman many have perished, and from this lust blazes up like fire.
verses.9:10: Every woman who is a prostitute will be trampled down like dung in the road.
verses.9:11: Many who marveled at the beauty of another man's wife have become reprobate, for her conversation blazes up like fire.
verses.9:12: Do not sit at all with another man's wife, nor recline with her on your elbow.
verses.9:13: And do not dispute with her over wine, or else your heart might turn aside to her, and with your blood you might slip into destruction.
verses.9:14: Do not abandon an old friend, for a new one will not be like him.
verses.9:15: A new friend is new wine; it will grow old, and with sweetness you will drink it.
verses.9:16: Do not be jealous of the glory and wealth of a sinner, for you do not know what his overthrow will be.
verses.9:17: Do not let the injustice of the unjust please you, knowing that even down to the underworld the ungodly man will not be pleasing.
verses.9:18: Stay far away from a man who has the power to kill, and you will not suspect the fear of death.
verses.9:19: And if you approach him, do not commit any offense, or else he might take away your life.
verses.9:20: Know the fellowship of death, for you will tread in the midst of snares, and you will walk upon the weapons of those who grieve.
verses.9:21: According to your strength, guard yourself against your neighbor, and confer with the wise and the prudent.
verses.9:22: Let righteous men be your table companions, and let your boasting be in the fear of God.
verses.9:23: And let the thought of God be in your understanding, and all your discourse in the precepts of the Most High.
verses.9:24: In the hand of craftsmen works will be praised, and a leader of the people in the wisdom of his speech, and in the understanding of older men, the word.
verses.9:25: A loose-tongued man is terrifying in his city, and one who is rash in his word will be detestable.
verses.10:1: A wise judge will judge his people, and the rule of a sensible man will be stable.
verses.10:2: As the judge of the people is, so also are his ministers; and as the ruler of the city is, such also are those who dwell in it.
verses.10:3: An unwise king will destroy his people, and cities will be inhabited through the good sense of the powerful.
verses.10:4: In the hand of God is the power of the earth, and He will raise up a useful ruler over it in due time.
verses.10:5: In the hand of God is a man's prosperity, and upon the face of the scribe He will place His honor.
verses.10:6: Do not remember any wrongdoing of a neighbor, and do nothing in works of wrongdoing.
verses.10:7: Pride is hateful before God and men, and all iniquity of the nations is detestable.
verses.10:8: A kingdom is transferred from nation to nation because of injustices, wrongs, outrages, and various deceits.
verses.10:9: But nothing is more wicked than a greedy man. Why are earth and ashes proud?
verses.10:10: Nothing is more unjust than to love money; for this man holds even his own soul for sale, because in his life he has cast away his innermost parts.
verses.10:11: All dominion is brief in life; a prolonged illness burdens the physician.
verses.10:12: A brief illness the physician cuts short; so too a king is today, and tomorrow he will die.
verses.10:13: For when a man dies, he will inherit serpents, beasts, and worms.
verses.10:14: The beginning of a man's pride is to fall away from God,
verses.10:15: because his heart has departed from Him who made him; for the beginning of all sin is pride. Whoever holds fast to it will be filled with curses, and it will overthrow him in the end.
verses.10:16: Therefore the Lord has dishonored the assemblies of evil men and has destroyed them to the end.
verses.10:17: God has torn down the thrones of proud leaders and made the meek sit in their place.
verses.10:18: God has dried up the roots of proud nations and planted the humble from those very nations.
verses.10:19: The Lord has overturned the lands of the nations and destroyed them down to the foundation.
verses.10:20: He has dried up some of them and utterly destroyed them, and has made their memory cease from the earth.
verses.10:21: God destroyed the memory of the proud and left the memory of those who are humble in mind.
verses.10:22: Pride was not created for men, nor wrath for the offspring of women.
verses.10:23: This seed of men will be honored, the one that fears God; but this seed will be dishonored, the one that transgresses the commandments of the Lord.
verses.10:24: In the midst of brothers their ruler is in honor, and those who fear the Lord will be in His eyes.
verses.10:25: The glory of the rich, the honored, and the poor is the fear of God.
verses.10:26: Do not despise a righteous poor man, and do not magnify a sinful rich man.
verses.10:27: The great man, the judge, and the powerful man are in honor, and no one is greater than the one who fears God.
verses.10:28: Free men will serve a sensible servant, and a prudent and disciplined man will not grumble when rebuked, and an ignorant man will not be honored.
verses.10:29: Do not lift yourself up in doing your work, and do not delay in a time of distress.
verses.10:30: Better is the one who works and abounds in all things than the one who boasts and lacks bread.
verses.10:31: Son, in gentleness preserve your soul, and give it honor according to its merit.
verses.10:32: Who will justify the one who sins against his own soul? And who will honor the one who dishonors his own soul?
verses.10:33: A poor man glories through his discipline and fear, and there is a man who is honored because of his wealth.
verses.10:34: But the one who glories in poverty, how much more in wealth! And let the one who glories in wealth fear poverty.
verses.11:1: The wisdom of the humbled man will exalt his head and make him sit in the midst of great men.
verses.11:2: Do not praise a man for his beauty, nor scorn a man for his appearance.
verses.11:3: Small among flying creatures is the bee, yet its fruit has the beginning of sweetness.
verses.11:4: Never glory in clothing, nor be lifted up in the day of your honor; for wondrous are the works of the Most High alone, and glorious, hidden, and unseen are His works.
verses.11:5: Many tyrants have sat on the throne, and an unsuspected man has worn the diadem.
verses.11:6: Many powerful men have been severely oppressed, and glorious men have been handed over into the hands of others.
verses.11:7: Before you inquire, do not blame anyone; and when you have inquired, rebuke justly.
verses.11:8: Before you hear, do not answer a word, and in the midst of speeches do not interject to speak.
verses.11:9: Do not contend about a matter that does not trouble you, and do not stand in the judgment of sinners.
verses.11:10: Son, do not let your activities be in many things; and if you become rich, you will not be free from offense. For if you pursue, you will not overtake; and you will not escape if you run ahead.
verses.11:11: There is a man laboring, hurrying, and grieving, an ungodly man, and all the more he will not abound.
verses.11:12: There is a feeble man in need of recovery, failing more in strength and abounding in poverty,
verses.11:13: and the eye of God has looked upon him for good, and raised him up from his lowliness, and exalted his head; and many have marveled at him and honored God.
verses.11:14: Good and evil, life and death, poverty and wealth are from God.
verses.11:15: Wisdom, discipline, and knowledge of the law are with God; love and the ways of the good are with Him.
verses.11:16: Error and darkness were created together with sinners, and those who exult in evil things grow old in evil.
verses.11:17: The gift of God abides with the righteous, and its progress will have success forever.
verses.11:18: There is one who grows rich by acting sparingly, and this is the portion of his reward,
verses.11:19: in that he says, "I have found rest for myself, and now I will eat from my goods alone."
verses.11:20: And he does not know that time will pass by, and death draws near, and he leaves everything to others, and he will die.
verses.11:21: Stand in your covenant, and converse in it, and grow old in the work of your commandments.
verses.11:22: Do not remain in the works of sinners, but trust in God and remain in your place.
verses.11:23: For it is easy in the eyes of God suddenly to enrich a poor man.
verses.11:24: The blessing of God hastens to the reward of the righteous, and in a swift hour its progress bears fruit.
verses.11:25: Do not say, "What need do I have? And what good things will be mine from this?"
verses.11:26: Do not say, "I am sufficient for myself, and how will I be harmed from this?"
verses.11:27: In the day of good things do not be unmindful of evil things, and in the day of evil things do not be unmindful of good things,
verses.11:28: for it is easy before God in the day of death to repay each one according to his ways.
verses.11:29: The affliction of an hour brings forgetfulness of great luxury, and at a man's end is the uncovering of his works.
verses.11:30: Before death do not praise any man, for in his children a man is recognized.
verses.11:31: Do not bring every man into your house, for many are the ambushes of the deceitful man.
verses.11:32: For just as the inward parts of stinking things belch forth, and as a partridge is brought into a cage, and as a roe deer into a snare, so also is the heart of the proud, and like a spy seeing the fall of his neighbor.
verses.11:33: For turning good things into evil things, he lies in ambush, and upon the chosen he will place a blemish.
verses.11:34: From one spark a fire is increased, and from one deceitful man blood is increased; and a sinful man lies in ambush for blood.
verses.11:35: Guard yourself against a pestilent man, for he devises evil things, or else he may bring mockery upon you forever.
verses.11:36: Admit a stranger to yourself, and he will overthrow you in a whirlwind, and he will estrange you from your own.
verses.12:1: If you do good, know to whom you do it, and there will be much gratitude for your good deeds.
verses.12:2: Do good to a righteous man, and you will find a great reward; and if not from him, certainly from the Lord.
verses.12:3: For it is not well with the one who is persistent in evils and does not give alms, because the Most High also hates sinners and has shown mercy to those who repent.
verses.12:4: Give to a merciful man, and do not support a sinner; and to the ungodly and to sinners He will repay vengeance, keeping them for the day of vengeance.
verses.12:5: Give to a good man, and do not receive a sinner.
verses.12:6: Do good to a humble man, and do not give to an ungodly man; forbid loaves of bread to be given to him, so that he may not become more powerful than you through them.
verses.12:7: For you will find double evils in all the good things that you ever do for him, because the Most High also hates sinners and will repay vengeance to the ungodly.
verses.12:8: A friend will not be recognized in prosperity, and an enemy will not be hidden in adversity.
verses.12:9: In a man's prosperity, his enemies are in sorrow; and in his adversity, a friend is recognized.
verses.12:10: Do not ever trust your enemy, for his wickedness corrodes like bronze.
verses.12:11: And even if he walks humbled and bowed down, apply your mind and guard yourself from him.
verses.12:12: Do not place him beside you, nor let him sit at your right hand, so that he may not perhaps turn into your place and seek your seat; and in the end you will recognize my words, and be stung by my sayings.
verses.12:13: Who will have pity on a charmer struck by a serpent, and on all who draw near to wild beasts? And so it is with him who keeps company with an unrighteous man and is wrapped up in his sins.
verses.12:14: For one hour he will remain with you; but if you turn aside, he will not endure.
verses.12:15: With his lips an enemy speaks sweetly, and in his heart he lies in wait to overthrow you into a pit.
verses.12:16: With his eyes an enemy weeps, and if he finds an opportunity, he will not be satisfied with blood.
verses.12:17: And if evils come upon you, you will find him there first.
verses.12:18: With his eyes an enemy weeps, and as though helping, he will undermine the soles of your feet.
verses.12:19: He will shake his head and clap his hands, and whispering many things, he will change his expression.
verses.13:1: Whoever touches pitch will be stained by it, and whoever associates with a proud man will put on pride.
verses.13:2: Whoever associates with one more honorable than himself takes a burden upon himself; and do not be a companion to one richer than yourself.
verses.13:3: What fellowship will a kettle have with an earthen pot? For when they strike against each other, it will be shattered.
verses.13:4: A rich man has acted unjustly, and he will rage; but a poor man, when wronged, will keep silent.
verses.13:5: If you give generously, he will take you in; and if you have nothing, he will abandon you.
verses.13:6: If you have anything, he will live with you and empty you out, and he himself will not grieve over you.
verses.13:7: If you are necessary to him, he will trip you up, and smiling, he will give hope, telling you good things, and he will say, "What do you need?"
verses.13:8: And he will put you to shame with his meals, until he drains you empty twice and three times; and in the end he will mock you, and afterward, seeing you, he will abandon you and shake his head at you.
verses.13:9: Humble yourself to God, and wait for His hands.
verses.13:10: Take care that you are not led astray into folly and humbled.
verses.13:11: Do not be humble in your wisdom, so that, being humbled, you are not led astray into folly.
verses.13:12: When invited by a more powerful man, withdraw; for because of this he will invite you all the more.
verses.13:13: Do not be intrusive, so that you may not be pushed back; and do not stay far from him, so that you may not pass into oblivion.
verses.13:14: Do not insist on speaking on equal terms with him, nor trust his many words; for through much talking he will test you, and smiling, he will question you about your secrets.
verses.13:15: His cruel mind will store up your words, and he will not hold back from malice and from chains.
verses.13:16: Be on your guard, and pay careful attention to your hearing, because you walk with your own overthrow.
verses.13:17: And hearing those things, see as in a dream, and you will be watchful.
verses.13:18: All your life love God, and call upon Him for your salvation.
verses.13:19: Every animal loves what is like itself, and so too every man loves the one nearest to him.
verses.13:20: All flesh will be joined to its like, and every man will become a companion to one like himself.
verses.13:21: If a wolf will ever associate with a lamb, so will a sinner with a righteous man.
verses.13:22: What association does a holy man have with a dog? Or what share does a rich man have with a poor man?
verses.13:23: A lion's prey is the wild donkey in the wilderness; so too the pastures of the rich are the poor.
verses.13:24: And just as humility is an abomination to a proud man, so also a poor man is the abhorrence of a rich man.
verses.13:25: A rich man, when shaken, is steadied by his friends; but a humble man, when he falls, will be driven away even by his acquaintances.
verses.13:26: For a rich man who is deceived, there are many rescuers; he has spoken proud things, and they have justified him.
verses.13:27: A humble man has been deceived, and moreover he is rebuked; he has spoken sensibly, and no place has been given to him.
verses.13:28: A rich man has spoken, and all have kept silent, and they will carry his word all the way to the clouds.
verses.13:29: A poor man has spoken, and they say, "Who is this?" And if he stumbles, they will overthrow him.
verses.13:30: Wealth is good in which there is no sin on the conscience, and poverty is most wicked in the mouth of an ungodly man.
verses.13:31: A man's heart changes his face, whether for good or for evil.
verses.13:32: You will find the trace of a good heart and a good face with difficulty, and with labor.
verses.14:1: Blessed is the man who has not slipped in word from his mouth, and has not been stung by the sorrow of transgression.
verses.14:2: Happy is he who has not had sorrow in his own mind, and has not fallen away from his hope.
verses.14:3: For a greedy and stingy man, wealth is without reason; and for an envious man, to what purpose is gold?
verses.14:4: Whoever heaps up unjustly from his own soul gathers for others, and in his goods another will live in luxury.
verses.14:5: Whoever is wicked to himself, to whom else will he be good? And he will not take delight in his own goods.
verses.14:6: Nothing is more wicked than he who begrudges himself, and this is the repayment of his malice.
verses.14:7: And even if he does good, he does it unknowingly and unwillingly; and in the end he reveals his malice.
verses.14:8: Wicked is the eye of an envious man, both turning away his face and despising his own soul.
verses.14:9: The eye of a greedy man is insatiable in a portion of iniquity; it will not be satisfied until it consumes his own soul, drying it up.
verses.14:10: An evil eye is directed toward evil things, and will not be filled with bread, but will be needy and in sorrow over its own table.
verses.14:11: Son, if you have anything, do good to yourself, and present worthy offerings to God.
verses.14:12: Remember that death does not delay, and remember the covenant of the underworld, because it has been shown to you; for the covenant of this world will surely die.
verses.14:13: Before death, do good to your friend, and according to your strength, reach out and give to a poor man.
verses.14:14: Do not be deprived of a good day, and do not let a small portion of a good gift pass you by.
verses.14:15: Will you not leave your pains and your labors to others in the division of the lot?
verses.14:16: Give and receive, and justify your soul.
verses.14:17: Before your death practice righteousness, because in the underworld there is no finding of food.
verses.14:18: All flesh will grow old like grass, and like a flourishing leaf on a green tree.
verses.14:19: Some are brought forth, and others are cast down; so is the generation of flesh and blood: one comes to an end, and another is born.
verses.14:20: Every corruptible work will fail in the end, and whoever works it will go with it.
verses.14:21: And every chosen work will be justified, and whoever works it will be honored in it.
verses.14:22: Blessed is the man who will dwell in wisdom, and who will meditate in his righteousness, and in understanding will ponder the watchfulness of God;
verses.14:23: who reflects on her ways in his heart and has understanding in his own secrets, going after her like a tracker and taking his stand in her ways;
verses.14:24: who looks through her windows and listens at her doors.
verses.14:25: He who rests near her house and drives a peg into her walls will set up his hut close by her hands, and good things will rest in his hut forever.
verses.14:26: He will place his children under her shelter, and under her branches he will dwell.
verses.14:27: He will be protected under her shelter from the heat, and in her glory he will rest.
verses.15:1: He who fears God will do what is good, and he who holds fast to righteousness will take hold of her,
verses.15:2: and she will meet him like an honored mother, and like a wife from her virginity she will receive him.
verses.15:3: She will feed him with the bread of life and understanding, and she will give him the water of saving wisdom to drink. And she will be made firm in him, and he will not be bent;
verses.15:4: and she will hold him fast, and he will not be put to shame; and she will exalt him among his neighbors,
verses.15:5: and in the midst of the assembly she will open his mouth, and she will fill him with the spirit of wisdom and understanding, and she will clothe him with a robe of glory.
verses.15:6: She will store up joy and exultation as treasure upon him, and she will give him an eternal name as an inheritance.
verses.15:7: Foolish people will not take hold of her, and sensible people will meet her. Foolish people will not see her, for she is far away from pride and deceit.
verses.15:8: Lying men will not be mindful of her, and truthful men will be found in her, and they will have success until the inspection of God.
verses.15:9: Praise is not becoming in the mouth of a sinner,
verses.15:10: because wisdom has come forth from God. For praise will stand beside the wisdom of God, and in a faithful mouth it will abound, and the Sovereign will give it to him.
verses.15:11: Do not say, "Through God she is absent," for what He hates, do not do.
verses.15:12: Do not say, "He has led me astray," for ungodly people are not needed by Him.
verses.15:13: The Lord hates every abomination of error, and it will not be lovable to those who fear Him.
verses.15:14: From the beginning God established man, and left him in the hand of his own deliberation.
verses.15:15: He added His commandments and precepts.
verses.15:16: If you wish to keep the commandments and to practice pleasing faithfulness forever, they will preserve you.
verses.15:17: He has placed water and fire before you; stretch out your hand to whichever you wish.
verses.15:18: Before man are life and death, good and evil; whatever pleases him will be given to him,
verses.15:19: for the wisdom of God is great, and He is strong in power, seeing everyone without ceasing.
verses.15:20: The eyes of the Lord are toward those who fear Him, and He Himself recognizes every work of man.
verses.15:21: He has commanded no one to act impiously, and He has given no one room to sin.
verses.15:22: For He does not desire a multitude of unfaithful and useless sons.
verses.16:1: Do not rejoice in ungodly sons if they are multiplied, nor take delight over them if the fear of God is not in them.
verses.16:2: Do not trust in their life, and do not look upon their labors.
verses.16:3: For one who fears God is better than a thousand ungodly sons,
verses.16:4: and it is better to die without children than to leave behind ungodly children.
verses.16:5: By one sensible man a homeland will be inhabited; the tribe of the ungodly will be deserted.
verses.16:6: My eye has seen many such things, and my ear has heard mightier things than these.
verses.16:7: In the congregation of sinners a fire will blaze up, and in an unbelieving nation wrath will flare up.
verses.16:8: The ancient giants, who were destroyed trusting in their own strength, did not gain pardon for their sins.
verses.16:9: And He did not spare the sojourning of Lot, and He detested them because of the pride of their word.
verses.16:10: He did not have mercy on them, destroying the whole nation, even as it exalted itself in its sins.
verses.16:11: And just as with the six hundred thousand foot soldiers, who were gathered together in the hardness of their heart; and if one had been stiff-necked, it would be a marvel if he had gone unpunished.
verses.16:12: For mercy and wrath are with Him; supplication is mighty, and He pours out wrath.
verses.16:13: According to His mercy, so His reproof judges people according to their works.
verses.16:14: The sinner will not escape with plunder, and the endurance of the one who practices mercy will not be delayed.
verses.16:15: All mercy will make room for each one according to the merit of his works, and according to the understanding of his sojourning.
verses.16:16: Do not say, "I will be hidden from God, and from on high, who will remember me?
verses.16:17: In a great people I will not be recognized; for what is my soul in so immense a creation?"
verses.16:18: Look, heaven and the heavens of heavens, the abyss, and the entire earth, and the things that are in them will be shaken in His sight.
verses.16:19: The mountains together, and the hills, and the foundations of the earth, when God looks upon them, will be violently shaken with trembling.
verses.16:20: And in all these things the heart is devoid of sense, and every heart is comprehended by Him.
verses.16:21: And who comprehends His ways, and the storm that not even the eye of man will see?
verses.16:22: For most of His works are in hidden places, yet who will declare the works of His righteousness, or who will endure them? For the covenant is far from some, and the questioning of all is at the end.
verses.16:23: He who is lacking in heart thinks empty things, and an unwise and erring man thinks foolish things.
verses.16:24: Listen to me, son, and learn the instruction of good sense, and pay attention to my words in your heart,
verses.16:25: and I will speak instruction in equity, and I will search diligently to recount wisdom; and pay attention to my words in your heart, and I speak in equity of spirit the powers that God placed in His works from the beginning, and in truth I declare His knowledge.
verses.16:26: In the judgment of God are His works from the beginning, and from their establishment He separated their parts, and their beginnings in their nations.
verses.16:27: He adorned their works forever; they neither hungered nor grew weary, and they did not cease from their works.
verses.16:28: Not one of them will crowd its neighbor forever.
verses.16:29: Do not be disbelieving of His word.
verses.16:30: After these things God looked upon the earth and filled it with His good things.
verses.16:31: Every living soul has made proclamation before its face, and into it again is their return.
verses.17:1: God created man from the earth, and according to His own image He made him.
verses.17:2: And He turned him back into it again, and according to Himself He clothed him with strength.
verses.17:3: He gave him a number of days and a time, and He gave him authority over the things that are on the earth.
verses.17:4: He placed the fear of him upon all flesh, and he had dominion over beasts and birds.
verses.17:5: He created from him a helper like himself; He gave them deliberation, and a tongue, and eyes, and ears, and a heart for thinking, and He filled them with the discipline of understanding.
verses.17:6: He created for them knowledge of the spirit, He filled their heart with discernment, and He showed them evil and good.
verses.17:7: He placed His eye upon their hearts, to show them the majesty of His works,
verses.17:8: so that they may praise the name of sanctification and glory in His wonders, so that they may recount the majesty of His works.
verses.17:9: He added discipline to them, and He gave them the law of life as an inheritance.
verses.17:10: He established an eternal covenant with them, and He showed them righteousness and His judgments.
verses.17:11: And their eye saw the majesty of His honor, and their ears heard the honor of the voice. And He said to them, "Be on guard against everything unjust."
verses.17:12: And He commanded them, each one concerning his neighbor.
verses.17:13: Their ways are always before Him; they are not hidden from His eyes.
verses.17:14: Over every nation He appointed a ruler.
verses.17:15: And Israel was made the manifest portion of God.
verses.17:16: And all their works are like the sun in the sight of God, and His eyes are looking upon their ways without ceasing.
verses.17:17: The covenants are not hidden by their iniquity, and all their iniquities are in the sight of God.
verses.17:18: The almsgiving of a man is like a signet with Him, and He will preserve the kindness of a man like the pupil of the eye.
verses.17:19: And afterward He will rise up and repay them retribution, to each one upon their own head, and He will turn them into the inner parts of the earth.
verses.17:20: But to those who repent He gave the way of righteousness, and He strengthened those who were failing to endure, and He appointed for them the lot of truth.
verses.17:21: Turn to the Lord, and abandon your sins.
verses.17:22: Pray before the face of the Lord, and lessen offenses.
verses.17:23: Return to the Lord, and turn away from your unrighteousness, and greatly hate abomination.
verses.17:24: And know the righteous deeds and judgments of God, and stand in the lot of the offering and of the prayer of the Most High God.
verses.17:25: Go into the parts of the holy age, with the living and those who give praise to God.
verses.17:26: Do not linger in the error of the ungodly; before death give praise; from a dead man, as from nothing, praise perishes.
verses.17:27: You will give praise while living; alive and whole you will give praise, and you will praise God and glory in His compassions.
verses.17:28: How great is the mercy of the Lord, and His forgiveness toward those who turn to Him!
verses.17:29: For not all things can be in men, since a son of man is not immortal, and they have taken pleasure in the vanity of malice.
verses.17:30: What is brighter than the sun? Yet even it will fail. Or what is more wicked than what flesh and blood has devised? And this will be reproved.
verses.17:31: He Himself looks upon the power of the height of heaven, and all men are earth and ashes.
verses.18:1: He who will live forever created all things together. God alone will be justified, and He remains an unconquered king forever.
verses.18:2: Who is sufficient to recount His works?
verses.18:3: For who will search out His mighty deeds?
verses.18:4: And who will declare the power of His greatness? Or who will go on to recount His mercy?
verses.18:5: It is not possible to diminish or to add, nor is it possible to find out the mighty deeds of God.
verses.18:6: When a man has finished, then he will begin; and when he has rested, he will be perplexed.
verses.18:7: What is man, and what is his grace? And what is his good, or what is his wickedness?
verses.18:8: The number of the days of men, at most one hundred years, has been reckoned like a drop of water from the sea; and like a pebble of sand, so are a few years in the day of eternity.
verses.18:9: Because of this, God is patient toward them, and He pours out His mercy upon them.
verses.18:10: He saw the presumption of their heart, that it is evil; and He knew their ruin, that it is wicked.
verses.18:11: Therefore He filled up His propitiation in them and showed them the way of equity.
verses.18:12: The compassion of a man is toward his neighbor, but the mercy of God is upon all flesh.
verses.18:13: He who has mercy teaches and instructs, like a shepherd his flock.
verses.18:14: He has compassion on the one who receives the teaching of compassion, and on the one who hastens in His judgments.
verses.18:15: Son, in good things do not give a complaint, and in every gift do not give the sadness of an evil word.
verses.18:16: Will not dew cool the scorching heat? So also is a word better than a gift.
verses.18:17: Look, is not a word above a good gift? Yet both are with a justified man.
verses.18:18: A fool will harshly reproach, and the gift of an undisciplined man makes the eyes waste away.
verses.18:19: Before judgment prepare righteousness for yourself, and before you speak, learn.
verses.18:20: Before sickness apply medicine, and before judgment question yourself, and in the sight of God you will find forgiveness.
verses.18:21: Before sickness humble yourself, and in the time of infirmity show your way of life.
verses.18:22: Do not be hindered from praying always, and do not be afraid to be justified until death, for the reward of God remains forever.
verses.18:23: Before prayer prepare your soul, and do not be like a man who tests God.
verses.18:24: Remember wrath in the day of consummation, and the time of retribution in the turning of the face.
verses.18:25: Remember poverty in the time of abundance, and the needs of poverty in the day of riches.
verses.18:26: From morning until evening the time will be changed, and all these things are swift in the eyes of God.
verses.18:27: A wise man will fear in all things, and in the days of offenses he will be on guard against sloth.
verses.18:28: Every astute man recognizes wisdom, and to the one who finds her he will give praise.
verses.18:29: Those who are discerning in words have themselves also acted wisely, and have understood truth and righteousness, and have rained down proverbs and judgments.
verses.18:30: Do not go after your desires, and turn away from your will.
verses.18:31: If you grant your soul its desires, it will make you a joy to your enemies.
verses.18:32: Do not take delight in crowds, nor in small ones, for their conflict is continual.
verses.18:33: Do not become poor in contention from borrowing at interest when you have nothing in your purse, for you will be envious of your own life.
verses.19:1: A worker given to drunkenness will not become wealthy, and the one who despises small things will gradually fall.
verses.19:2: Wine and women cause the wise to apostatize, and they will convict the sensible.
verses.19:3: And the one who joins himself to prostitutes will be wicked; decay and worms will inherit him, and he will be lifted up as a greater example, and his soul will be taken away from the number.
verses.19:4: The one who believes quickly is fickle in heart and will be diminished, and the one who offends against his own soul will be held in contempt.
verses.19:5: The one who rejoices in iniquity will be denounced, and the one who hates reproof will be shortened in life, and the one who hates talkativeness extinguishes evil.
verses.19:6: The one who sins against his own soul will repent, and the one who takes delight in wickedness will be denounced.
verses.19:7: Do not repeat a wicked and harsh word, and you will not be diminished.
verses.19:8: Do not tell your thoughts to friend and enemy, and if you have a fault, do not lay it bare.
verses.19:9: For he will hear you and watch you, and as though defending the sin, he will hate you, and so he will always be present with you.
verses.19:10: Have you heard a word against your neighbor? Let it die within you, confident that it will not burst you apart.
verses.19:11: Because of a word a fool is in labor, like the groaning of the birth of an infant.
verses.19:12: An arrow lodged in a thigh of flesh: so is a word in the heart of a fool.
verses.19:13: Reprove a friend, in case he has not understood and says, "I did not do it," or, if he has done it, so that he does not go on to do it again.
verses.19:14: Reprove a neighbor, in case he has not said it, and if he has said it, so that he may not repeat it.
verses.19:15: Reprove a friend, for often slander occurs.
verses.19:16: And do not believe every word. There is one who slips with his tongue, yet not from the heart.
verses.19:17: For who is there who has not offended with his tongue? Reprove a neighbor before you threaten him,
verses.19:18: and give place to the fear of the Most High, for all wisdom is the fear of God, and in it is to fear God, and in all wisdom is the ordering of the law.
verses.19:19: And the discipline of wickedness is not wisdom, and the thinking of sinners is not prudence.
verses.19:20: There is wickedness, and in it is an abomination, and there is a foolish person who is diminished in wisdom.
verses.19:21: Better is a man who is diminished in wisdom and lacking in understanding, in fear, than one who abounds in understanding and transgresses the law of the Most High.
verses.19:22: There is an exact cleverness, and it itself is unjust.
verses.19:23: And there is one who utters an exact word, declaring the truth. There is one who wickedly humbles himself, and his inward parts are full of deceit.
verses.19:24: And there is one who submits himself excessively from much humility, and there is one who bows his face and pretends not to see what is unknown.
verses.19:25: And if by weakness of strength he is prevented from sinning, if he finds a time for doing evil, he will do evil.
verses.19:26: From appearance a man is known, and from the meeting of the face a sensible man is known.
verses.19:27: The clothing of the body, and the laughter of the teeth, and the gait of a man tell about him.
verses.19:28: There is a lying reproof in the anger of an abusive man, and there is a judgment that is not proved to be good, and there is one who keeps silent, and he is prudent.
verses.20:1: How good it is to rebuke rather than to be angry, and not to hinder the one who confesses in prayer!
verses.20:2: The lust of a eunuch will deflower a young woman;
verses.20:3: so is the one who executes an unjust judgment by force.
verses.20:4: How good it is for one who has been reproved to display repentance! For in this way you will escape voluntary sin.
verses.20:5: There is one who keeps silent who is found to be wise, and there is a detestable person who is brash in speaking.
verses.20:6: There is one who keeps silent, not having understanding of speech, and there is one who keeps silent, knowing the proper time.
verses.20:7: A wise man will keep silent until the time, but the unrestrained and the imprudent will not observe the time.
verses.20:8: The one who uses many words will harm his own soul, and the one who takes authority for himself unjustly will be hated.
verses.20:9: There is advancement in evils for an undisciplined man, and there is a finding leading to loss.
verses.20:10: There is a gift that is not useful, and there is a gift whose repayment is double.
verses.20:11: There is diminishment because of glory, and there is one who will lift up his head from lowliness.
verses.20:12: There is one who buys many things at a small price and pays them back sevenfold.
verses.20:13: A wise man makes himself lovable in words, but the favors of fools will be poured out.
verses.20:14: The gift of a foolish person will not be useful to you, for his eyes are sevenfold.
verses.20:15: He will give little and reproach much, and the opening of his mouth is a blaze.
verses.20:16: Today someone lends at interest, and tomorrow he demands it back; a man of this kind is detestable.
verses.20:17: A fool will have no friend, and there will be no gratitude for his good things.
verses.20:18: For those who eat his bread are of a false tongue. How often and how many will mock him!
verses.20:19: For he did not distribute with right understanding what was to be held, and likewise what was not to be held.
verses.20:20: The slip of a false tongue is like one falling on a pavement; so the fall of evil people will come swiftly.
verses.20:21: An ungracious man is like an empty tale; it will be continually in the mouth of the undisciplined.
verses.20:22: From the mouth of a fool a proverb will be rejected, for he does not speak it in its own time.
verses.20:23: There is one who is prevented from sinning because of poverty, and in his rest he will be stung.
verses.20:24: There is one who will destroy his own soul because of shame, and because of an imprudent person he will destroy it, and by partiality toward a person he will destroy himself.
verses.20:25: There is one who because of shame makes a promise to a friend and has gained him as an enemy for nothing.
verses.20:26: A lie is a wicked reproach in a man, and it will be continually in the mouth of the undisciplined.
verses.20:27: Better is a thief than the persistence of a lying man, yet both will inherit destruction.
verses.20:28: The ways of lying men are without honor, and their shame is with them without ceasing.
verses.20:29: A wise man will advance himself in words, and a prudent man will please the great.
verses.20:30: The one who works his land will raise high a heap of crops, and the one who works righteousness will himself be exalted, and the one who pleases the great will escape iniquity.
verses.20:31: Presents and gifts blind the eyes of judges, and like a mute person, it turns aside their reproofs in the mouth.
verses.20:32: Hidden wisdom and an unseen treasure: what usefulness is in both?
verses.20:33: Better is the one who conceals his foolishness than a man who hides his wisdom.
verses.21:1: Son, you have sinned; do not add to it again, but also plead concerning your former sins, so that they may be forgiven you.
verses.21:2: As from the face of a serpent, flee from sins, and if you come near to them, they will take hold of you.
verses.21:3: Its teeth are the teeth of a lion, slaying the souls of men.
verses.21:4: Like a two-edged broadsword is all iniquity; for its wound there is no healing.
verses.21:5: Berating and wrongs will bring wealth to nothing, and a house that is overly rich will be brought to nothing by pride; so the wealth of a proud person will be uprooted.
verses.21:6: The plea of a poor person will reach from the mouth all the way to His ears, and judgment will come swiftly to him.
verses.21:7: Whoever hates correction is a footprint of a sinner, and whoever fears God will turn back to his own heart.
verses.21:8: One who is powerful with a bold tongue is known from afar, and a sensible person knows that he slips from him.
verses.21:9: Whoever builds his house at the expense of others is like one who gathers his stones in winter.
verses.21:10: Tow gathered together is the congregation of those who sin, and their end is a flame of fire.
verses.21:11: The way of sinners is made smooth with stones, and at their end are the underworld, and darkness, and punishments.
verses.21:12: Whoever keeps righteousness will retain its understanding.
verses.21:13: The completion of the fear of God is wisdom and understanding.
verses.21:14: Whoever is not wise in what is good will not be instructed.
verses.21:15: Yet there is a wisdom that abounds in evil, and there is no understanding where there is bitterness.
verses.21:16: The knowledge of a wise person will abound like a flood, and his counsel remains like a spring of life.
verses.21:17: The heart of a fool is like a shattered vessel, and it will not hold any wisdom.
verses.21:18: Whatever wise word a knowledgeable person hears, he will praise it and add it to himself; a self-indulgent person has heard it, and it will displease him, and he will throw it behind his back.
verses.21:19: The discourse of a fool is like a burden on the road, whereas on the lips of a sensible person grace will be found.
verses.21:20: The mouth of a prudent person is sought in the assembly, and they will ponder his words in their hearts.
verses.21:21: Like a ruined house, so is wisdom to a fool, and the knowledge of a senseless person is inexplicable words.
verses.21:22: Instruction to a fool is shackles on the feet, and like bonds for the hands on the right hand.
verses.21:23: A fool raises his voice in laughter, but a wise man will scarcely laugh quietly.
verses.21:24: Instruction to a prudent person is a golden ornament, and like an armlet on the right arm.
verses.21:25: The foot of a fool is quick into a neighbor's house, and an experienced person will feel shame before the presence of a powerful man.
verses.21:26: A fool will look from a window into a house, but a well-instructed man will stand outside.
verses.21:27: It is the foolishness of a person to listen through a door, and a prudent person will be weighed down by disgrace.
verses.21:28: The lips of the imprudent will speak foolish things, but the words of the prudent will be weighed on a scale.
verses.21:29: In the mouth of fools is their heart, and in the heart of the wise is their mouth.
verses.21:30: While an ungodly person curses the devil, he himself curses his own soul.
verses.21:31: A whisperer will defile his own soul, and he will be hated in all things, and whoever stays with him will be detestable; a quiet and sensible person will be honored.
verses.22:1: With a muddy stone a lazy person has been stoned, and everyone will speak about the scorn for him.
verses.22:2: With ox dung a lazy person has been stoned, and everyone who touches him will shake off his hands.
verses.22:3: A father's shame is over an undisciplined son, and a daughter will turn out to be a loss.
verses.22:4: A prudent daughter is an inheritance to her husband, whereas one who brings shame becomes a disgrace to the one who fathered her.
verses.22:5: A brazen woman brings shame upon father and husband, and she will not be less than the ungodly; and by both she will be dishonored.
verses.22:6: Music in mourning is untimely discourse; lashes and instruction are wisdom at all times.
verses.22:7: Whoever teaches a fool is like one who glues together a potsherd.
verses.22:8: Whoever speaks a word to one who is not listening is like one who rouses a sleeper from deep sleep.
verses.22:9: One who recounts wisdom to a fool speaks with a sleeper, and at the end of the discourse he says, "Who is this?"
verses.22:10: Weep over a dead person, for his light has failed; and weep over a fool, for understanding has failed.
verses.22:11: Weep a little over a dead man, because he has found rest;
verses.22:12: for the most wicked life of a most wicked man is worse than the death of a fool.
verses.22:13: Mourning for a dead person is seven days, but for a fool and an ungodly person it is all the days of their life.
verses.22:14: Do not speak much with a fool, and do not go with a senseless person.
verses.22:15: Guard yourself from him, so that you may not have trouble, and you will not be defiled by his sin.
verses.22:16: Turn aside from him, and you will find rest, and you will not grow weary in his folly.
verses.22:17: What will be heavier than lead? And what other name is there for it than fool?
verses.22:18: Sand and salt and a mass of iron are easier to bear than a person who is imprudent and foolish and ungodly.
verses.22:19: A wooden tie-beam bound into the foundation of a building will not come apart; so also is a heart established in the thought of counsel.
verses.22:20: The thought of a sensible person will at no time be corrupted by fear.
verses.22:21: Just as stakes on high places, and rough stones laid without mortar, will not remain against the face of the wind.
verses.22:22: So also a timid heart in the thought of a fool will not withstand the onslaught of fear.
verses.22:23: Just as a trembling heart in the thought of a fool will at no time fear, so also the one who remains in the precepts of God always.
verses.22:24: One who pricks an eye draws forth tears, and whoever pricks a heart brings forth feeling.
verses.22:25: One who throws a stone at birds will bring them down; so also one who reviles a friend dissolves friendship.
verses.22:26: Against a friend, even if you have drawn a sword, do not despair, for there is a return. Against a friend,
verses.22:27: if you have opened a bitter mouth, do not be afraid, for there is reconciliation, except for reviling, and reproach, and pride, and the revealing of a secret, and a treacherous blow; in all these things a friend will flee.
verses.22:28: Keep faith with a friend in his poverty, so that you may also rejoice in his good things.
verses.22:29: In the time of his affliction remain faithful to him, so that you may also be a co-heir in his inheritance.
verses.22:30: Before the fire of a furnace vapor and smoke of fire rise high; so also before bloodshed are curses, and insults, and threats.
verses.22:31: I will not be ashamed to greet a friend; I will not hide myself from his face, and if evils happen to me through him, I will endure.
verses.22:32: Everyone who hears will guard himself against him.
verses.22:33: Who will place a guard over my mouth, and a sure seal upon my lips, so that I may not fall because of them and my tongue may not destroy me?
verses.23:1: Lord, Father and Ruler of my life, do not abandon me in their counsel, and do not allow me to fall in them.
verses.23:2: Who will place whips upon my thought, and the instruction of wisdom upon my heart, so that they may not spare me for their acts of ignorance, and their offenses may not appear,
verses.23:3: and so that my acts of ignorance may not grow greater, nor my offenses be multiplied, nor my sins abound, and so that I may not fall in the sight of my adversaries, and my enemy may not rejoice over me?
verses.23:4: Lord, Father and God of my life, do not abandon me in their thought.
verses.23:5: Do not give me haughtiness of my eyes, and turn every desire away from me.
verses.23:6: Take away from me the cravings of the belly, and do not let the cravings of sexual union seize me, and do not hand me over to an irreverent and senseless soul.
verses.23:7: Listen to the instruction of the mouth, children, and the one who keeps it will not perish by his lips, nor stumble in the most wicked deeds.
verses.23:8: In his vanity the sinner is caught, and the proud and the reviler will stumble in them.
verses.23:9: Do not let your mouth become accustomed to swearing, for there are many falls in it.
verses.23:10: And let the naming of God not be continual in your mouth, and do not mingle with the names of the holy ones, because one will not be free from guilt regarding them.
verses.23:11: For just as a slave continually interrogated is not lacking in bruising, so everyone who swears and invokes in everything will not be cleansed from sin.
verses.23:12: A man who swears much will be filled with iniquity, and a scourge will not depart from his house.
