verses.44:23: and to exalt his seed like the stars, and to give them an inheritance from sea to sea, and from the river to the ends of the earth.
verses.44:24: And in Isaac He acted in the same manner, for the sake of Abraham his father.
verses.44:25: The Lord gave him the blessing of all nations, and confirmed the covenant upon the head of Jacob.
verses.44:26: He acknowledged him in His blessings, and gave him an inheritance, and divided for him a portion among twelve tribes.
verses.44:27: And He preserved for him men of mercy, finding favor in the eyes of all flesh.
verses.45:1: Beloved by God and men was Moses, whose memory is in blessing.
verses.45:2: He made him similar in the glory of the holy ones, and He magnified him in the fear of enemies, and by his words he calmed portents.
verses.45:3: He glorified him in the sight of kings, and commanded him before His people, and showed him His glory.
verses.45:4: In his faithfulness and gentleness He made him holy, and chose him out of all flesh.
verses.45:5: For He heard him and his voice, and brought him into the cloud.
verses.45:6: And He gave him the precepts face to face, and the law of life and instruction, to teach Jacob His covenant and Israel His judgments.
verses.45:7: He made his brother Aaron exalted, and like him, from the tribe of Levi.
verses.45:8: He established for him an eternal covenant, and gave him the priesthood of the nation, and blessed him in glory;
verses.45:9: and He encircled him with a sash of glory, and clothed him in a robe of glory, and crowned him with instruments of strength.
verses.45:10: He placed on him a foot-length robe, and undergarments, and a shoulder garment, and surrounded him with very many golden bells all around,
verses.45:11: to give a sound in his walking, to make a sound heard in the temple as a memorial for the children of his nation.
verses.45:12: A holy robe of gold, and blue, and purple, the woven work of a wise man endowed with judgment and truth;
verses.45:13: with twisted scarlet, the work of a craftsman, with precious stones fashioned in a setting of gold and engraved by the work of a stonecutter, for a memorial according to the number of the tribes of Israel.
verses.45:14: A golden crown upon his turban, stamped with the sign of holiness and glory of honor: a work of strength, and adorned desires of the eyes.
verses.45:15: There were no such things so beautiful before him, all the way to the beginning.
verses.45:16: No outsider was clothed with it, but only his own sons alone and his descendants throughout all time.
verses.45:17: His sacrifices were consumed by fire daily.
verses.45:18: Moses filled his hands, and anointed him with holy oil.
verses.45:19: It was made for him an eternal covenant, and for his seed, like the days of heaven, to perform the priesthood, and to have praise, and to glorify his people in His name.
verses.45:20: He chose him from all the living to offer sacrifice to God, incense and a pleasing aroma, for a memorial, to make atonement for His people;
verses.45:21: and He gave him authority in His precepts, in the covenants of judgments, to teach Jacob the testimonies and in His law to give light to Israel.
verses.45:22: For outsiders stood against him, and because of envy men surrounded him in the wilderness, those who were with Dathan and Abiram, and the congregation of Korah in wrath.
verses.45:23: The Lord God saw, and it did not please Him, and they were consumed in the fury of wrath.
verses.45:24: He worked portents against them and consumed them in a flame of fire.
verses.45:25: And He added glory to Aaron, and gave him an inheritance, and He allotted to him the firstfruits of the produce of the land.
verses.45:26: First of all, He prepared bread for them to the full; for they will also eat the sacrifices of the Lord, which He gave to him and to his seed.
verses.45:27: However, in the land he will not inherit nations, and there is no portion for him in the nation; for He Himself is his portion and inheritance.
verses.45:28: Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, is third in glory, by imitating him in the fear of the Lord,
verses.45:29: and standing in the reverence of the nation; in the goodness and eagerness of his soul he pleased God for Israel.
verses.45:30: Therefore He established for him a covenant of peace, as ruler of the holy things and of his nation, so that the dignity of the priesthood might belong to him and to his seed forever.
verses.45:31: And a covenant for King David, the son of Jesse, from the tribe of Judah, an inheritance for him and for his seed, so that He might give wisdom into our heart, to judge His nation in righteousness, so that their good things would not be wiped out; and He made their glory eternal for their nation.
verses.46:1: Mighty in war was Joshua son of Nave, successor of Moses among the prophets, who was great according to his name,
verses.46:2: greatest for the salvation of the chosen of God, to conquer the enemies rising up, so that he might obtain the inheritance of Israel.
verses.46:3: What glory he attained in raising his hands and brandishing swords against the cities!
verses.46:4: Who before him stood so firm? For the Lord Himself brought forth the enemies.
verses.46:5: Was not the sun held back in his wrath, and one day made like two?
verses.46:6: He called upon the Most High, the Mighty One, in fighting against enemies on every side; and the great and holy God heard him with hailstones of exceedingly strong power.
verses.46:7: He made an assault against the hostile nation, and on the descent He destroyed the adversaries,
verses.46:8: so that the nations might know His power, because it is not easy to fight against God. And he followed behind the Mighty One.
verses.46:9: And in the days of Moses he showed mercy, he and Caleb the son of Jephunneh, to stand against the enemy, and to restrain the nation from sins, and to break the grumbling of malice.
verses.46:10: And those two who were appointed were delivered from danger out of the number of six hundred thousand foot soldiers, to bring them into the inheritance, into a land that flows with milk and honey.
verses.46:11: And the Lord gave might to Caleb himself, and even into old age strength remained with him, so that he ascended to the high place of the land, and his seed obtained the inheritance,
verses.46:12: so that all the sons of Israel might see that it is good to obey the holy God.
verses.46:13: And the judges, each by his own name, whose heart was not corrupted, who did not turn away from the Lord,
verses.46:14: may their memory be in blessing, and may their bones sprout from their place.
verses.46:15: And may their name remain forever, remaining to their children, the glory of holy men.
verses.46:16: Beloved by the Lord his God, Samuel, the prophet of the Lord, renewed the kingdom, and anointed rulers in his nation.
verses.46:17: In the law of the Lord he judged the congregation, and God saw Jacob; and in his faithfulness he was proven a prophet,
verses.46:18: and in his words he was known to be faithful, because he saw the God of light.
verses.46:19: And he called upon the Lord Almighty in fighting against enemies standing around on every side, in the offering of an unblemished lamb.
verses.46:20: And the Lord thundered from heaven, and with a great sound He made His voice heard,
verses.46:21: and He crushed the rulers of the Tyrians and all the leaders of the Philistines.
verses.46:22: And before the time of the end of his life and of the age, he bore testimony in the sight of the Lord and of the anointed one: he did not accept money, even down to sandals, from any flesh, and no man accused him.
verses.46:23: And after this he fell asleep; and he made known to the king and showed him the end of his life; and he lifted up his voice from the earth in prophecy, to blot out the ungodliness of the nation.
verses.47:1: After these things Nathan arose, a prophet in the days of David.
verses.47:2: And like fat separated from the flesh, so was David from the sons of Israel.
verses.47:3: He played with lions as with lambs, and with bears he did likewise, as with lambs of the sheep, in his youth.
verses.47:4: Did he not kill the giant and take away reproach from the nation?
verses.47:5: In raising his hand, with a stone from a sling he cast down the boasting of Goliath.
verses.47:6: For he called upon the Lord Almighty, and He granted in his right hand to remove a man mighty in war, and to exalt the horn of his nation.
verses.47:7: Thus He glorified him in ten thousands, and praised him in the blessings of the Lord, in offering him a crown of glory;
verses.47:8: for he crushed enemies on every side, and uprooted the opposing Philistines until the present day; he crushed their horn forever.
verses.47:9: In every work he gave thanksgiving to the Holy One and to the Most High, in a word of glory.
verses.47:10: With all his heart he praised the Lord, and he loved God who made him, and He gave him power against enemies.
verses.47:11: And he made singers stand before the altar, and with their sound he made sweet melodies.
verses.47:12: And he gave splendor in the celebrations, and adorned the seasons until the completion of life, so that they might praise the holy name of the Lord and magnify the holiness of God in the morning.
verses.47:13: The Lord purged his sins and exalted his horn forever; and He gave him a covenant of the kingdom and a throne of glory in Israel.
verses.47:14: After him arose a discerning son, and because of him he cast down all the power of the enemies.
verses.47:15: Solomon reigned in days of peace, to whom God subjected all enemies, so that he might build a house in His name and prepare holiness forever. How you were instructed in your youth,
verses.47:16: and you were filled, like a river, with wisdom, and your soul uncovered the earth.
verses.47:17: And you filled riddles with comparisons; to the islands far away your name was spread abroad, and you were loved in your peace.
verses.47:18: At songs, and proverbs, and comparisons, and interpretations, the lands marveled,
verses.47:19: and at the name of the Lord God, whose title is the God of Israel.
verses.47:20: You gathered gold like brass, and like lead you piled up silver.
verses.47:21: And you bowed your thighs to women; you had authority over your body.
verses.47:22: You put a blemish on your glory, and profaned your seed, to bring wrath upon your children and for your folly to be stirred up,
verses.47:23: so that you made the kingdom divided in two, and a harsh kingdom to rule from Ephraim.
verses.47:24: But God will not abandon His mercy, and He will not ruin nor blot out His works, nor will He destroy from the root the descendants of His chosen one; and He will not ruin the seed of him who loves the Lord.
verses.47:25: Yet He gave a remnant to Jacob, and to David from that very stock.
verses.47:26: And Solomon came to his end with his fathers.
verses.47:27: And he left behind him from his seed the folly of the nation,
verses.47:28: and one lacking in prudence, Rehoboam, who turned the nation away by his counsel;
verses.47:29: and Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel sin and gave Ephraim a way of sinning; and their very many sins overflowed.
verses.47:30: They greatly turned them away from their land.
verses.47:31: And he sought out all wickednesses until vengeance came upon them, and He delivered them from all sins.
verses.48:1: And Elijah the prophet rose up like fire, and his word was burning like a torch.
verses.48:2: He brought a famine upon them, and those provoking him by their envy became few, for they could not endure the commands of the Lord.
verses.48:3: By the word of the Lord he held back heaven, and he cast down fire from heaven three times.
verses.48:4: Thus Elijah was magnified in his wondrous deeds. And who can boast in the same way as you?
verses.48:5: You who raised up a dead person from the underworld, from the lot of death, by the word of the Lord God;
verses.48:6: who cast down kings to destruction, and easily shattered their power, and cast down glorious men from their bed;
verses.48:7: who hear judgment at Sinai, and at Horeb judgments of vindication;
verses.48:8: who anoint kings to repentance, and make prophets successors after you;
verses.48:9: who were received up in a whirlwind of fire, in a chariot of fiery horses;
verses.48:10: who are recorded in the judgments of the times to calm the anger of the Lord, to reconcile a father's heart to his son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob.
verses.48:11: Blessed are those who saw you and were adorned in your friendship.
verses.48:12: For we live by life only; after death, however, our name will not be such.
verses.48:13: Elijah indeed was hidden in a whirlwind, and in Elisha his spirit was made full; in his days he did not fear any prince, and no one overcame him by power;
verses.48:14: nor did any word surpass him, and his dead body prophesied.
verses.48:15: In his life he performed marvels, and in death he worked wondrous deeds.
verses.48:16: In all these things the people did not repent, and they did not turn away from their sins, until they were cast out from their land and scattered into every land;
verses.48:17: and a very small nation was left, and a prince in the house of David.
verses.48:18: Some of them did what pleased God, while others committed many sins.
verses.48:19: Hezekiah fortified his city and brought water into the midst of it; he dug through the rock with iron and built a well for the water.
verses.48:20: In his days Sennacherib came up and sent Rabshakeh, and he lifted up his hand against them; he raised his hand against Zion and became proud in his power.
verses.48:21: Then their hearts and hands were shaken, and they suffered pain like women in labor.
verses.48:22: And they called upon the merciful Lord, and spreading out their hands, lifted them up to heaven; and the Holy One, the Lord God, quickly heard their voice.
verses.48:23: He did not remember their sins, nor did He give them over to their enemies, but He cleansed them by the hand of Isaiah the holy prophet.
verses.48:24: He cast down the camp of the Assyrians, and the angel of the Lord crushed them;
verses.48:25: for Hezekiah did what pleased God, and walked firmly in the way of his father David, which Isaiah commanded him, a great prophet and faithful in the sight of God.
verses.48:26: In his days the sun went backward, and he added life to the king.
verses.48:27: By a great spirit he saw the last things, and he comforted those mourning in Zion forever.
verses.48:28: He showed things to come, and hidden things before they happened.
verses.49:1: The memory of Josiah is made into a blend of fragrance, the work of a perfumer.
verses.49:2: In every mouth his memory will be sweetened like honey, and like music at a banquet of wine.
verses.49:3: He himself was divinely directed to the repentance of the nation, and he took away the abominations of impiety.
verses.49:4: And he guided his heart to the Lord, and in the days of sinners he strengthened piety.
verses.49:5: Except for David and Hezekiah and Josiah, all committed sin.
verses.49:6: For the kings of Judah abandoned the law of the Most High and despised the fear of God.
verses.49:7: For they gave their own kingdom to others, and their own glory to a foreign nation.
verses.49:8: They burned the chosen city of holiness and made its streets desolate, by the hand of Jeremiah.
verses.49:9: For they mistreated him who from his mother's womb was consecrated a prophet, to overthrow, and to uproot, and to destroy, and again to build and to renew.
verses.49:10: Ezekiel, who saw the vision of glory that He showed him on the chariot of the cherubim.
verses.49:11: For he made mention of the enemies in the rain, to do good to those who showed the right ways.
verses.49:12: And may the bones of the twelve prophets sprout from their place; for they strengthened Jacob, and they redeemed themselves in the faith of strength.
verses.49:13: How shall we magnify Zerubbabel? For he also is like a signet on the right hand,
verses.49:14: so also Jeshua, son of Jozadak, who in their days built the house and raised up a holy temple to the Lord, prepared for everlasting glory.
verses.49:15: And Nehemiah is in memory for a long time, who raised up for us the overthrown walls, and made the gates and bars stand, who raised up our houses.
verses.49:16: No one has been born on earth such as Enoch, for he himself was also received up from the earth;
verses.49:17: nor like Joseph, who was born a man, prince of his brothers, support of the nation, ruler of his brothers, mainstay of the people;
verses.49:18: and his bones were visited, and after death they prophesied.
verses.49:19: Seth and Shem attained glory among men, and above every soul in origin is Adam.
verses.50:1: Simon, son of Onias, the high priest, who in his life shored up the house, and in his days strengthened the temple.
verses.50:2: The height of the temple also was founded by him, the double structure and the lofty walls of the temple.
verses.50:3: In his days the wells of water flowed forth, and like the sea they were filled beyond measure.
verses.50:4: He cared for his nation and delivered it from destruction;
verses.50:5: he prevailed in enlarging the city, attained glory in the company of the nation, and enlarged the entrance of the house and of the court.
verses.50:6: Like the morning star in the midst of a cloud, and like the full moon, he shines in his days;
verses.50:7: and like the radiant sun, so he shone forth in the temple of God.
verses.50:8: Like a radiant rainbow among clouds of glory, and like the bloom of roses in the days of spring, and like lilies that are by a passage of water, and like fragrant frankincense in the days of summer;
verses.50:9: like fire shining forth, and frankincense burning in the fire;
verses.50:10: like a vessel of solid gold, adorned with every precious stone;
verses.50:11: like a sprouting olive tree and a cypress lifting itself on high, when he received the robe of glory and was clothed in the perfection of strength.
verses.50:12: At the ascent of the holy altar, he gave glory to the vestment of holiness.
verses.50:13: And when he received the portions from the hand of the priests, while he himself stood beside the altar and around him was a crown of brothers, like a planting of cedar on Mount Lebanon,
verses.50:14: so they stood around him like branches of a palm tree, and all the sons of Aaron in their glory.
verses.50:15: And the offering of the Lord was in their hands before the whole assembly of Israel; and performing the completion at the altar, to magnify the offering of the Most High King,
verses.50:16: he stretched out his hand in the libation and poured out from the blood of the grape.
verses.50:17: He poured out at the foundation of the altar a divine fragrance to the Prince on high.
verses.50:18: Then the sons of Aaron shouted aloud; they sounded on hammered trumpets and made a loud voice heard as a remembrance before God.
verses.50:19: Then all the people hastened together and fell on their faces upon the ground, to worship the Lord their God and to offer prayers to Almighty God Most High.
verses.50:20: And the singers swelled their voices, and in the great house a sound full of sweetness was increased.
verses.50:21: And the people petitioned the Lord Most High in prayer, until the honor of the Lord was completed and they completed their service.
verses.50:22: Then descending, he raised his hands over the whole congregation of the sons of Israel, to give glory to God from his lips and to boast in His name;
verses.50:23: and he repeated his prayer, wishing to show the power of God.
verses.50:24: And now pray to the God of all, who accomplished great things throughout the whole earth, who increased our days from the womb of our mother, and dealt with us according to His mercy:
verses.50:25: may He grant us gladness of heart, and that there be peace in our days in Israel throughout everlasting days;
verses.50:26: that Israel may trust that the mercy of God is with us, so that He may deliver us in His days.
verses.50:27: Two nations my soul hates, and the third, which I hate, is not a nation:
verses.50:28: those who dwell on Mount Seir, and the Philistines, and the foolish people who live in Shechem.
verses.50:29: Jesus, son of Sirach, of Jerusalem, who renewed wisdom from his heart, wrote in this book the instruction of wisdom and discipline.
verses.50:30: Blessed is he who occupies himself with these good things; he who sets them in his heart will always be wise.
verses.50:31: For if he does these things, he will be strong for all things, because the light of God is his path.
verses.51:1: The prayer of Jesus son of Sirach. I will give thanks to You, Lord, King, and I will extol You, God my Savior.
verses.51:2: I will give thanks to Your name, because You have become a helper and protector to me,
verses.51:3: and have rescued my body from destruction, from the snare of a wicked tongue, and from the lips of those who practice falsehood; and in the sight of those standing by, You have become a helper to me.
verses.51:4: And You delivered me, according to the multitude of the mercy of Your name, from the roaring ones prepared for food,
verses.51:5: from the hands of those seeking my soul, and from the gates of the tribulations that surrounded me;
verses.51:6: from the pressure of the flame that surrounded me, and in the middle of the fire I was not scorched;
verses.51:7: from the depth of the belly of the underworld, and from a defiled tongue, and from a word of falsehood, from a wicked king, and from an unjust tongue.
verses.51:8: My soul will praise the Lord until death.
verses.51:9: And my life was drawing near to the underworld below.
verses.51:10: They surrounded me on every side, and there was no one to help; I was looking for the help of people, and there was none.
verses.51:11: I remembered Your mercy, Lord, and Your work, which are from ages past.
verses.51:12: Because You rescue those who wait for You, Lord, and You deliver them from the hands of the nations.
verses.51:13: You exalted my dwelling above the earth, and I pleaded because of death flowing down.
verses.51:14: I called upon the Lord, the Father of my Lord, that He would not abandon me in the day of my distress, and in the time of the proud, without help.
verses.51:15: I will praise Your name continually, and I will extol it in thanksgiving; and my prayer was heard.
verses.51:16: And You delivered me from destruction and rescued me from an unjust time.
verses.51:17: Therefore I will give thanks, and I will speak praise to You, and I will bless the name of the Lord.
verses.51:18: While I was still young, before I wandered about, I sought wisdom openly in my prayer.
verses.51:19: Before the temple I was asking for them, and even to the very end I will seek it out; and it blossomed like an early-ripening grape.
verses.51:20: My heart rejoiced in it; my foot walked a straight path; from my youth I kept searching for it.
verses.51:21: I inclined my ear a little, and received it.
verses.51:22: I found much wisdom in myself, and I made much progress in it.
verses.51:23: To Him who gives me wisdom I will give glory.
verses.51:24: For I resolved to practice it. I was zealous for good, and I will not be put to shame.
verses.51:25: My soul wrestled in it, and in practicing it I was strengthened.
verses.51:26: I stretched out my hands on high, and I mourned her ignorance.
verses.51:27: I directed my soul toward it, and in knowledge I found it.
verses.51:28: With her I gained a heart from the beginning; because of this, I will not be abandoned.
verses.51:29: My belly was in turmoil while seeking it; therefore I will possess a good possession.
verses.51:30: The Lord gave me a tongue as my reward, and with it I will praise Him.
verses.51:31: Draw near to me, you uninstructed, and gather yourselves into the house of instruction.
verses.51:32: Why do you still delay? And what do you say about these things? Your souls thirst intensely.
verses.51:33: I opened my mouth and spoke: "Buy for yourselves without silver,
verses.51:34: and put your neck under the yoke, and let your soul receive instruction; for it is near at hand to find it.
verses.51:35: See with your eyes that I labored a little, and found much rest for myself.
verses.51:36: Take up instruction with a great sum of silver, and possess abundant gold in it.
verses.51:37: Let your soul rejoice in His mercy, and you will not be put to shame in His praise.
verses.51:38: Do your work before the time, and He will give you your reward in His time."

notes.1:1: Stage 1 restored the Latin Translator's Prologue prefixed to Sirach 1:1 in Clem1598-USFX; Latin 'quando inter se dicuntur' (lit. "when they are spoken among/in themselves") refers to reading those scriptures in their original tongue. In the closing sentence, Vulgate "ante ævum" ("before eternity" or "before the age") is a distinct Latin reading where the Greek has "forever" ("eis ton aiōna"), and the Vulgate also adds "God" ("Deo") after "the Lord."
notes.1:8: The Vulgate expands this verse with "Most High, almighty Creator, and a mighty King" and "a ruling God," where the Greek reads simply "There is one who is wise, greatly to be feared, sitting upon His throne."
notes.1:9: The phrase "in the Holy Spirit" ("in Spiritu Sancto") is a distinct Vulgate reading not found in the Greek text.
notes.1:14: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 1:14 (Vulgate/LXX-II expansion without a separate Saints slot).
notes.1:15: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 1:15, replacing the prior empty-alignment placeholder.
notes.1:16: Vulgate "it walks with chosen women" ("cum electis feminis graditur") is a distinct Latin reading diverging from the Greek (1:15), which speaks of Wisdom laying an eternal foundation among human beings.
notes.1:17: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 1:17 (Vulgate/LXX-II expansion); Latin 'religiositas' denotes religious devotion or piety (likewise in 1:18, 1:26).
notes.1:18: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 1:18 (Vulgate/LXX-II expansion).
notes.1:19: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 1:19 (parallel doublet of 1:13, reading 'in diebus consummationis illius', "in the days of his completion/end", rather than 1:13's 'in die defunctionis suæ').
notes.1:21: Vulgate "a generationibus" ("with produce," literally "from yields/generations") reflects an Old Latin rendering of Greek "genēmata" ("produce"), and the Vulgate's wording here (native 1:21; Saints 1:17) and in native 1:20 (Saints 1:16, "fullness is from her fruits") differs from the Greek.
notes.1:24: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 1:24 (parallel to Saints/Greek 1:19).
notes.1:26: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 1:26 (Vulgate-distinct doublet ahead of 1:32 / Saints 1:25).
notes.1:27: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 1:27 (parallel to Saints/Greek 1:21).
notes.2:1: The clause "stand in righteousness and fear" ("sta in justitia et timore") is a Vulgate addition absent from the Greek; Latin "tentationem" ("temptation") carries the broad sense of both trial/testing and temptation.
notes.2:2: The clause "incline your ear, and receive words of understanding" is a Vulgate addition; "obductionis" ("calamity," literally "a covering over" or "a bringing upon") is an Old Latin calque of Greek "epagōgē" ("calamity/affliction").
notes.2:3: The opening command "Endure the delays of God" ("Sustine sustentationes Dei," literally "endure the deferrals/sustainings of God") is a Vulgate addition not present in the Greek.
notes.2:10: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 2:10 (Vulgate/LXX-II expansion parallel to Saints 2:9).
notes.2:11: Vulgate "nationes hominum" ("the nations of men") reflects an Old Latin rendering of Greek "archaias geneas" ("ancient generations") and adds "sons" ("filii"); the two rhetorical questions that follow in Greek 2:10b now stand in restored native Vulgate 2:12.
notes.2:12: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 2:12 (parallel to the second half of Saints/Greek 2:10; previously claimed absent in the note on old 2:10).
notes.2:17: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 2:17 (parallel to Saints/Greek 2:14b).
notes.2:22: The Vulgate adds "saying, 'If we do not repent'" ("dicentes: Si pœnitentiam non egerimus"), absent from the Greek, framing the verse as a conditional statement.
notes.2:23: The Vulgate adds "with Him" ("cum ipso est") at the end.
notes.3:1: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 3:1 (Vulgate-distinct opening verse before 3:2 = Saints 3:1).
notes.3:4: Vulgate uniquely reads "He who loves God" (Qui diligit Deum) and adds the final two clauses, whereas the Greek reads "He who honors a father atones for sins." Latin exorabit pro peccatis means to appease or obtain pardon by prayer for sins, and in oratione dierum is literally "in the prayer of days" (daily prayer).
notes.3:10: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 3:10 (continuing 3:9 = Saints 3:8).
notes.3:16: Vulgate distinctly reads pro peccato matris ("in place of a mother's sin"), whereas the Greek reads simply "in place of sins" without mentioning a mother.
notes.3:22: Vulgate reads operibus ejus ("His works," referring to God, repeated in native 3:24 / Saints 3:23), whereas the Greek refers to "your works" (one's own tasks).
notes.3:28: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 3:28 (Vulgate/LXX-II expansion between 3:27 and 3:29).
notes.3:30: Vulgate renders Greek epagoge ("calamity/affliction") as Synagogae ("assembly/synagogue") and adds the closing clause et non intelligetur ("and it will not be understood").
notes.3:34: Vulgate uniquely adds et Deus prospector est ("and God is the watcher over"), making God the subject who remembers the person who returns a favor, whereas the Greek does not mention God here.
notes.4:1: Vulgate reads eleemosynam pauperis ("a poor man of his alms"), whereas the Greek reads "the livelihood of the poor."
notes.4:5: Vulgate adds propter iram ("because of anger") and renders the second clause literally as non relinquas quaerentibus tibi retro maledicere ("do not leave it to those who ask to curse you behind your back").
notes.4:11: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 4:11 (continuing 4:10 = Saints 4:10).
notes.4:12: Vulgate reads vitam inspirat ("breathes life into") and adds et praeibit in via justitiae ("and will go ahead in the way of righteousness"), whereas the Greek reads "Wisdom exalts her sons."
notes.4:17: Latin creaturae illius (literally "his creatures/offspring," rendering Greek geneai, "descendants") and in confirmatione ("in steadfastness/firm establishment") reflect Late Latin usage; in native 4:18 (Saints 4:17) Vulgate reads "in testing she walks with him, and at first she chooses him," whereas the Greek speaks of walking on crooked paths.
notes.4:19: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 4:19 (parallel to Saints/Greek 4:17).
notes.4:21: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 4:21 (continuing 4:20 = Saints 4:18).
notes.4:24: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 4:24 (parallel to Saints/Greek 4:20b).
notes.4:26: Latin accipere faciem is a literal biblical idiom for showing partiality or deference, here governing both faciem ("face") and mendacium ("lie"); Vulgate reads "against your own face" and "a lie," whereas the Greek reads "against your own soul" and "to your downfall."
notes.4:27: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 4:27 (parallel to Saints/Greek 4:22b, continuing into 4:28).
notes.5:1: Latin adds "unjust" (iniquas) and the closing clause "for it will profit nothing in the time of vengeance and calamity" (in tempore vindictae et obductionis), both absent in the standard Greek text. The Latin noun obductio (literally "a bringing-upon" or "covering over," calquing Greek epagoge) denotes affliction or calamity (also in 5:8).
notes.5:3: Latin "How was I able?" (Quomodo potui?) is a Vulgate-distinct reading where the Greek has "Who will have power over me?" The closing phrase "will surely take vengeance" translates the emphatic Latin participle-and-verb idiom vindicans vindicabit (literally "avenging, will avenge").
notes.5:5: All five Sixto-Clementine Vulgate witnesses unanimously print 'De propitiatio peccato' (understood as a historic variant of 'propitiato peccato', "concerning a propitiated/forgiven sin"), differing from the Greek "concerning atonement."
notes.5:7: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 5:7 (continuing 5:6 = Saints 5:6).
notes.5:9: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 5:9 (continuing 5:8 = Saints 5:7).
notes.5:13: Vulgate "Be gentle in hearing" (Esto mansuetus ad audiendum) is a distinct Latin reading where the Greek has "Be swift to hear."
notes.5:18: Vulgate "Do justice to small and great alike" (Justifica pusillum et magnum similiter, literally "Justify the small and the great alike") differs from the Greek "In great and small matters do not err."
notes.6:12: This verse is a notable Vulgate-distinct reading: the Latin turns it into a positive promise about a humble, deferential friend ("If he humbles himself before you [contra te] ... you will have a good friendship of one mind"), whereas the Greek warns of a false friend turning against one who is brought low.
notes.6:16: Vulgate "and immortality" (et immortalitatis) is a distinct Latin expansion where the Greek reads only "a medicine of life."
notes.6:20: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 6:20 (parallel to Saints/Greek 6:19b); Latin 'de generationibus illius' (lit. "from her yields/generations") follows the established rendering "produce" (cf. 1:21 / Saints 1:17).
notes.6:22: Latin "Like the strength of a stone, the testing will be upon them" (Quasi lapidis virtus probatio erit in illis) literally renders the Greek image of a heavy lifting-stone used as a test of strength.
notes.6:23: Latin adds "of instruction" (doctrinae) to "wisdom" and concludes with the Vulgate-distinct promise "she remains even to the presence of God" (permanet usque ad conspectum Dei).
notes.6:31: Vulgate "the beauty of life" (decor vitae) and "a saving binding" (alligatura salutaris, conveying both healing and salvation) are distinct Latin readings where the Greek describes "a golden ornament" and "a blue cord."
notes.7:5: The middle clause ('for He Himself is the knower of the heart') is a Vulgate-distinct expansion not found in the shorter Greek text.
notes.7:11: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 7:11 (parallel to Saints/Greek 7:9, previously missing from the critical text).
notes.7:13: The Vulgate reads 'amare' ('love'), likely an early Latin transmission variant for 'arare' ('plow,' matching the Greek metaphor of devising a lie).
notes.7:18: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 7:18 (parallel to Saints/Greek 7:16b).
notes.7:20: The Vulgate 'pecuniam differentem' ('who delays money,' i.e., puts off payment) is a distinct reading reflecting the Greek term 'diaphoron' ('gain' or 'money').
notes.7:28: Following the Clementine Vulgate verse division, the prepositional phrase 'With all your heart' stands at the end of native 7:28 (Saints 7:26) and governs 'honor your father' at the start of native 7:29 (Saints 7:27).
notes.7:33: The phrase 'purify yourself with the arms' ('propurga te cum brachiis') is a Vulgate-distinct reading; 'brachiis' (literally 'arms') reflects the sacrificial shoulder-portions given to the priests in the Greek text.
notes.7:34: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 7:34 (continuing 7:33 = Saints 7:31).
notes.7:35: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 7:35 (continuing 7:34 = Saints 7:31b); Latin 'brachiorum' literally means "arms" (reflecting the sacrificial shoulder-portions, as in 7:33).
notes.8:3: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 8:3 (parallel to Saints/Greek 8:2b).
notes.8:8: The closing clause ('and do not wish to become a cause of rejoicing,' literally 'and we do not wish to come into joy') is a Vulgate-distinct addition expressing unwillingness to become an object of others' gloating at death.
notes.8:10: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 8:10 (continuing 8:9 = Saints 8:8).
notes.8:12: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 8:12 (continuing 8:11 = Saints 8:9).
notes.8:13: The Vulgate expands the verse with 'by rebuking them' and 'of their sins,' creating a Latin wordplay on 'peccatorum' ('of sinners') and 'peccatorum' ('of sins').
notes.8:17: The Vulgate distinctly states 'for he judges according to what is just,' whereas the Greek text warns that others will judge in the judge's favor according to his standing.
notes.8:20: The Vulgate reads 'they will not be able to love anything except what pleases them,' diverging from the Greek text's statement that fools cannot keep a matter secret.
notes.9:1: In the Vulgate, the wife is the subject of 'ostendat' ('so that she does not show against you the malice of a wicked teaching'), whereas the Greek text warns the husband not to teach her an evil lesson against himself.
notes.9:5: The Vulgate 'in decore illius' ('by her beauty') is a distinct reading where the Greek text refers to incurring her legal penalties.
notes.9:9: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 9:9 (parallel to Saints/Greek 9:8b).
notes.9:10: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 9:10 (Vulgate placement matching the proverb of Greek 9:6b).
notes.9:11: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 9:11 (Vulgate expansion parallel to 9:8-9).
notes.9:13: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 9:13 (continuing 9:12 = Saints 9:9).
notes.9:15: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 9:15 (parallel to Saints/Greek 9:10b).
notes.9:17: The Vulgate distinctly reads 'the injustice of the unjust' and 'will not be pleasing,' differing from the Greek text's 'delight of the ungodly' and 'will not be justified.'
notes.9:20: The Vulgate adds 'Know the fellowship of death' and reads 'the weapons of those who grieve' ('dolentium arma'), a striking Vulgate divergence from the Greek text's 'battlements of a city.'
notes.9:24: The closing phrase 'and in the understanding of older men, the word' ('in sensu vero seniorum verbum') is a Vulgate-distinct third clause added to the proverb.
notes.10:8: The Vulgate reads "various deceits" (diversos dolos), whereas the Greek Septuagint has "wealth" (chremata).
notes.10:10: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 10:10 (parallel to Saints/Greek 10:9b).
notes.10:11: The Vulgate distinctly opens this verse with "All dominion is brief in life" (Omnis potentatus brevis vita) and arranges the surrounding sayings differently from the Greek.
notes.10:12: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 10:12 (parallel to Saints/Greek 10:10b).
notes.10:16: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 10:16 (parallel to Saints/Greek 10:13b).
notes.10:23: Unlike the Greek Septuagint's question-and-answer format, the Vulgate renders this verse as two parallel declarative statements.
notes.10:34: The Vulgate warns that one who glories in wealth should fear poverty (et qui gloriatur in substantia, paupertatem vereatur), whereas the Greek speaks of one who is dishonored in wealth being even more dishonored in poverty.
notes.11:5: The Vulgate reads "on the throne" (in throno), contrasting with the Greek Septuagint reading "on the ground" (epi edaphous).
notes.11:10: The Vulgate reads "if you become rich" (si dives fueris) and "if you run ahead" (si praecucurreris), whereas the Greek has "if you multiply them" and "if you flee."
notes.11:14: Latin honestas literally denotes honor or dignity, here used in the Late Latin sense of material wealth or prosperity opposite paupertas ("poverty").
notes.11:20: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 11:20 (continuing 11:19 = Saints 11:19).
notes.11:22: The Vulgate reads "Do not remain" (Ne manseris), whereas the Greek Septuagint reads "Do not marvel" (me thaumaze).
notes.11:23: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 11:23 (parallel to Saints/Greek 11:21b); Late Latin 'honestare' means "to enrich" or "to endow with prosperity/honor" (matching 'honestas' in 11:14).
notes.11:32: The Vulgate includes distinctive images not found in the Greek Septuagint, adding "the inward parts of stinking things belch forth" and "as a roe deer into a snare."
notes.12:3: The closing words 'et misertus est poenitentibus' ("and has shown mercy to those who repent") have no counterpart in the Greek.
notes.12:6: Latin 'panes' ("loaves of bread") is plural, which accounts for the plural pronoun 'in ipsis' ("through them").
notes.12:9: Vulgate 'amicus agnitus est' ("a friend is recognized") differs notably from the Greek ("even a friend will withdraw"); Latin 'malitia' here means "adversity" or "misfortune," paralleling 'in malis' in 12:8.
notes.12:12: Vulgate 'conversus in locum tuum' ("turn into your place") differs from the Greek ("having overthrown you").
notes.12:16: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 12:16 (parallel to Saints/Greek 12:16b).
notes.12:18: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 12:18 (Vulgate doublet continuing 12:17 = Saints 12:17; Latin 'suffodiet plantas tuas' literally means "will dig beneath your soles/heels").
notes.13:2: Vulgate reads a positive clause ('Pondus super se tollat', literally "would/let him take a burden upon himself"), whereas the Greek has a negative command ("Do not lift a burden beyond yourself").
notes.13:3: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 13:3 (parallel to Saints/Greek 13:2b).
notes.13:9: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 13:9 (Vulgate/LXX-II expansion before 13:10 = Saints 13:8).
notes.13:11: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 13:11 (Vulgate/LXX-II expansion following 13:10 = Saints 13:8).
notes.13:14: Latin 'Ne retineas' renders Greek 'me epeche' and here carries the sense "do not insist on" or "do not persist in" rather than "do not hold back from."
notes.13:17: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 13:17 (continuing 13:16 = Saints 13:13).

notes.17:27: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 17:27 (parallel to Saints/Greek 17:28b).

notes.18:11: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 18:11 (parallel to Saints/Greek 18:12b).
notes.18:13: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 18:13 (parallel to Saints/Greek 18:13b).

notes.18:24: All five Sixto-Clementine Vulgate witnesses read 'conversatione' here as a late-Latin variant of 'conversione' ("turning", rendering Greek apostrophe, "turning away of the face"; VulgSistina 1590 prints 'facies'), whereas in 18:21 'conversationem' carries its usual Latin sense of "way of life, conduct."
notes.18:32: Latin in turbis ... commissio ("in crowds ... conflict") is a Vulgate-distinct rendering where the Greek warns against delighting in great luxury and its expense (symbole, which can mean either "contribution" or "clash, encounter").

notes.19:3: The Vulgate expands this verse with the doublet "he will be lifted up as a greater example, and his soul will be taken away from the number" (extolletur in exemplum majus, et tolletur de numero anima ejus), where the standard Greek text has a single clause ("a reckless soul will be taken away").
notes.19:8: The Vulgate reads "if you have a fault, do not lay it bare" (si est tibi delictum, noli denudare), omitting the negation found in the Greek ("unless it is a sin for you"); in v. 9 the Vulgate also adds the distinctive phrase "as though defending the sin" (quasi defendens peccatum) where the Greek has "in due time."
notes.19:15: Late Latin commissio literally means a "setting at variance" or "offense," used here in the sense of slander or false report (corresponding to Greek diabole).
notes.19:18: The Vulgate distinctively reads "fear of the Most High" (timori Altissimi), "fear of God" (timor Dei), the added clause "and in it is to fear God," and "the ordering of the law" (dispositio legis), where the Greek reads "law of the Most High," "fear of the Lord," and "doing of the law."

notes.20:16: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 20:16 (parallel to Saints/Greek 20:15b).

notes.20:21: The Vulgate retains the untranslated Greek loanword acharis ("ungracious" or "graceless") and reads "an empty tale" (fabula vana) where the Greek has "an untimely tale."
notes.20:23: The Vulgate omits the negation present in the Greek ("will not be pricked by remorse"), reading affirmatively that "in his rest he will be stung" (stimulabitur).

notes.26:18: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 26:18 (parallel to Saints/Greek 26:14b).

notes.27:3: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 27:3 (Vulgate/LXX-II continuation of 27:2 = Saints 27:2).
notes.27:5: The Vulgate reads pulvis ("dust") and the Greek loanword aporia ("perplexity" or "distress"), whereas the Greek Septuagint reads "refuse" and "rubbish."

notes.27:12: The Vulgate reads Homo sanctus in sapientia manet sicut sol ("A holy man remains in wisdom like the sun"), whereas the Greek Septuagint reads "The discourse of a godly person is always wisdom."
notes.27:19: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 27:19 (parallel to Saints/Greek 27:16-17).

notes.28:28: The Vulgate reads aures tuas ("your ears," vs. Greek "your property"), adds "do not listen to a wicked tongue," and places "doors and bars" here (native 28:28 = Saints 28:24) rather than in native 28:29 (Saints 28:25), where the Vulgate instead reads confla ("melt down") and frenos ori tuo rectos ("proper bridles for your mouth").

notes.32:23: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 32:23 (continuing 32:22 = Saints 32:18); Latin 'insectationibus' denotes pursuits, attacks, or followings.

notes.33:29: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 33:29 (parallel to Saints/Greek 33:27b).

notes.34:11: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 34:11 (parallel to Saints/Greek 34:10b); Late Latin 'implanatus' renders Greek 'peplanemenos' ("having wandered / been led astray").

notes.43:1: Vulgate 'pulchritudo ejus' ('His beauty', continuing the reference to the Lord's glory in 42:25, or possibly 'its beauty', referring to the height) differs from the Greek, which reads 'the expanse of purity'.

notes.47:5: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 47:5 (parallel to Saints/Greek 47:4b).
notes.47:7: Vulgate uses singular verbs ('glorificavit', 'laudavit'), continuing the Lord from native 47:6 (Saints 47:5) as subject (or referring collectively to the nation), whereas the Greek has plural ('they glorified him... and praised him').
notes.47:10: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 47:10 (parallel to Saints/Greek 47:8b).
notes.47:15: Latin 'sanctitatem' ('holiness'), here in native 47:15 (Saints 47:13) and in native 47:12 (Saints 47:10), literally renders Greek 'hagiasma' ('sanctuary').
notes.47:16: Latin 'retexit' ('uncovered' or 'revealed') stands where the Greek reads 'covered' ('ekalypsen').
notes.47:20: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 47:20 (parallel to Saints/Greek 47:18b); Latin 'auricalcum' denotes brass/orichalcum (where Greek has 'tin').
notes.47:21: Vulgate reads active 'potestatem habuisti' ('you had authority') where the Greek uses the passive ('you were brought under dominion' or 'enslaved').
notes.47:25: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 47:25 (parallel to Saints/Greek 47:22b).
notes.47:31: Vulgate has singular 'quaesivit' ('he sought out') where the Greek is plural, uses 'defensio' (lit. 'defense/vindication') for Greek 'vengeance,' and adds the closing clause 'et ab omnibus peccatis liberavit eos' ('and He delivered them from all sins'), which is absent from the Greek.
notes.48:2: Vulgate reads 'those provoking him by their envy became few, for they could not endure the commands of the Lord,' whereas the Greek reads 'by his zeal he made them few in number' and lacks the closing clause.
notes.48:6: All five Sixto-Clementine Vulgate witnesses unanimously print the historic spelling 'pernicem' (for 'perniciem', "destruction") and include the clause "and easily shattered their power," absent from the standard Greek.
notes.48:8: Vulgate reads 'to repentance' (ad poenitentiam) and plural 'prophets' (prophetas), whereas the Greek has 'for retribution' and singular 'a prophet.'
notes.48:11: Vulgate reads 'were adorned in your friendship' (decorati sunt, reflecting the Greek variant kekosmenoi); the following clause stands in restored native Vulgate 48:12 ('For we live by life only; after death, however, our name will not be such'), contrasting with the Greek 'for we too shall surely live.'
notes.48:12: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 48:12 (parallel to Saints/Greek 48:11b; previously claimed absent in the note on 48:11). Vulgate 'Nam nos vita vivimus tantum: post mortem autem non erit tale nomen nostrum' diverges sharply from Greek "for we too shall surely live."
notes.48:18: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 48:18 (parallel to Saints/Greek 48:16).
notes.48:23: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 48:23 (parallel to Saints/Greek 48:20b).
notes.48:27: Vulgate attaches 'forever' (usque in sempiternum) to the end of native 48:27 (Saints 48:24), whereas in the Greek the phrase opens 48:25 ('to the end of time he revealed what was to occur').
notes.49:1: Native Vulgate ends 49:1 after 'the work of a perfumer' and places the lines comparing Josiah's memory to honey and banquet music in restored native Vulgate 49:2 (together corresponding to Saints/Greek 49:1).
notes.49:2: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 49:2 (parallel to Saints/Greek 49:1b; previously claimed omitted in the note on 49:1).
notes.49:6: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 49:6 (continuing 49:5 = Saints 49:4b).
notes.49:11: Following the Greek (which misread Hebrew 'Job' as 'enemies'), Vulgate reads 'the enemies in the rain' and renders the closing clause 'who showed the right ways' (Greek: 'who kept straight ways').
notes.49:12: Vulgate reads reflexive 'redeemed themselves in the faith of strength' (redemerunt se in fide virtutis), whereas the Greek has 'delivered them by confident hope.'
notes.49:17: Vulgate doubles the Greek epithets for Joseph ('prince of his brothers, support of the nation, ruler of his brothers, mainstay of the people').
notes.49:18: Vulgate adds 'and after death they prophesied,' absent from the standard Greek.
notes.49:19: Vulgate reverses the Greek order ('Shem and Seth') to 'Seth and Shem' and renders Greek 'in creation' as in origine ('in origin').
notes.50:3: Vulgate reads 'the wells of water flowed forth, and like the sea they were filled beyond measure,' where the Greek describes quarrying a bronze reservoir like the circumference of the sea.
notes.50:5: Vulgate renders the Greek phrase describing Simon's emergence from the sanctuary veil ('as he came out of the house of the veil') as 'and enlarged the entrance of the house and of the court.'
notes.50:10: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 50:10 (parallel to Saints/Greek 50:9b).
notes.50:12: Vulgate translates Greek peribolen ('enclosure/court') in its alternative sense of 'garment' as amictum ('vestment'), hence 'he gave glory to the vestment of holiness.'
notes.50:17: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 50:17 (parallel to Saints/Greek 50:15b).
notes.50:23: Vulgate keeps Simon as singular subject ('he repeated his prayer, wishing to show the power of God'), whereas the Greek has the people bowing down a second time to receive the blessing.
notes.50:26: Vulgate renders the verse with an infinitive clause ('that Israel may trust...') and reflexive in diebus suis, which grammatically refers to God ('His days'), though the Greek autou may refer to Simon's lifetime.
notes.51:4: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 51:4 (parallel to Saints/Greek 51:3a, previously missing from the critical text).
notes.51:5: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 51:5 (parallel to Saints/Greek 51:3b).
notes.51:7: Vulgate a rege iniquo ("from a wicked king") is a Vulgate-distinct reading where the Greek text speaks of a slanderous report to a king. Syntactically, the prepositional phrases in native 51:6-7 (Saints 51:4-5) depend on the verb of deliverance restored in native 51:4 (Saints 51:3).
notes.51:9: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 51:9 (continuing 51:8 = Saints 51:6).
notes.51:12: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 51:12 (continuing 51:11 = Saints 51:8).
notes.51:13: Vulgate pro morte defluente ("because of death flowing down") reflects a Vulgate-distinct rendering of Greek rhyseos as derived from rheo ("flow") rather than rhyomai ("deliver," as in "deliverance from death").
notes.51:14: Vulgate Dominum patrem Domini mei ("the Lord, the Father of my Lord") follows the Greek textual tradition rather than the Hebrew ("O Lord, you are my father").
notes.51:16: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 51:16 (continuing 51:15 = Saints unplaced 51:11 / Greek 51:11b-12a).
notes.51:19: Vulgate pro illis ("for them") is a Vulgate-distinct plural where the Greek has singular "for her" (wisdom), and effloruit ("it blossomed") supplies a finite verb rather than the Greek prepositional phrase "from the blossom."
notes.51:23: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 51:23 (parallel to Saints/Greek 51:17b).
notes.51:26: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 51:26 (parallel to Saints/Greek 51:19b); Latin 'insipientiam ejus' literally means "her/its foolishness (or ignorance)" (where Greek reads "my ignorances of her").
notes.51:27: Vulgate in agnitione ("in knowledge") is a Vulgate-distinct reading where the Greek text reads "in purification."
notes.51:28: Restored native Clementine Vulgate verse 51:28 (parallel to Saints/Greek 51:20b).
